reviews.reviewbody:
I has been a while since I listened to a straight audience tape, 1st official release, then a matrix then mainly soundboard, but I have to say this reminded of back in the day riding around in a truck windows down and the good ol grateful dead blaring.

1st set is short but sweet, always like a feels like a stranger opener.  Birdsong is again explorative and better then the one at Kaiser in February which was one of the highlights of that three night run.  Band is together tonight.

Second set is strong with a sweet Terrapin and a great jam in the transition portion of the song, a favorite of mine from the early to mid 80s.  Smokestack lightening has an extended jam on the end of it that is mind left the body tinged. Great stuff here. solid Stella with an short but aggressive Jerry solo that hints at the searing pace he featured this year.  Second Day job of the year, better then first but uninspired.

Underrated show if you ask me, there is a lot here.

metadata.notes:
I'll apologize upfront for the lack of archival information of this source.  I made  a cassette copy of this show when I was in college 20 some odd years ago from a cassette of unknown generation.  When I bought my first computer with a CD burner back in 1999 I transferred the cassette recording to CD.  Since I have never seen a SBD copy of this show circulate over the years and no SBD seed is listed in the etree database, I thought I'd post it for those interested (and just maybe a cleaner seed will surface as result?).  The recording has enough hiss, warble, pops, and clicks to make the pure audiophile cringe, but don't let it scare you - I was thrilled to get my hands on a SBD of this quality 20+ years ago.  It's just easy to get spoiled by the quality that circulates today.

As for the show itself, I've always felt that it was underrated.  The setlist is fairly typical of a tour opener, but the playing is crisp and clean throughout and the band shows lots of energy.  Nothing particularly stands out in the first set, but the band is tight showing no signs of sloppiness.  The China -> Rider has always been one of my favorites.  The Playin' in the Band -> Drums -> Space is absolutely fantastic.  I've always felt the best Drums -> Space were played in 1985 and this show supports that opinion.  Great show for Brent, he really tears up the second set!  For me, some shows just emote the feeling the band is genuinely happy to be there and this show is one of them.

Alabama Getaway beginning cuts and the quality of the recording is a little rough, but improves.

The jam in Playing in the Band is spectacular and the original taper must have thought so too, having broke it out as a separate jam on the tape cover, which I honored in the transfer to CD.  The jam actually extends 3 minutes into Drums.

Two second cut in Drums at 6:22 (tape flip?)

Jerry teases with the first few notes of St. Stephen during Space.

Around and Around has small cut at 2:33.

J.B. Goode end is cut and Day Job is missing.

reviews.reviewbody: They should ALWAYS be left intact...always
reviews.reviewtitle: Thanx but NEVER cut a Playin' jam!

reviews.reviewbody: I'm not one for using personal experience as the basis of my reviews, or in the production of my weekly radio show (Dead Zone, WRHU.ORG, Tuesdays, 7-9pm), but I this show calls for an exception to the rule. Why? well, it's not simply because Hampton VA turned out to be anything but the bucolic Virginia my buddy and I imagined as we made our way down from the oh so idyllic Rose Hill in the gritty Bronx.  There's not much to say about Hampton VA, unfortunately, although the Coliseum was small and had a barn-like quality to the sound.  But I digress!  What makes this show special is something as seemingly trivial as the t-shirt Jerry was wearing that night.  Well, trivial aside from the fact that it was BRIGHT RED! and not the customary black.  Indeed, the Red t-shirt was, as far as I know, worn by Jerry for the first time at this show, a signifier for his recent run-in with the law in Golden Gate park, or so it was thought.  Listen carefully to the energy in Jerry's voice during 'Alabama' and you hear what I'm saying.  He was a bit 'edgy' to say the least!  And the show was full of energy from top to bottom.  Too bad there are some gaps, cause it is truly one of the hidden gems in the archives!

The Reviewer said: "Jerry teases with the first few notes of St. Stephen during Space."

I was at this show, as well as having seen St. Stephen, and I think this statement is totally wrong. There are only 12 notes on the guitar (and any western instrument) and F# is one of them. F# is the first two notes of St. Stephen. You could say than he teased this on every space as it is hard to avoid an F# when your noodling during space for 8-10 minutes, running up & down the fretboard with only 12 notes to play. I'v played guitar professionally for 35 years and have a very good ear (especially for Dead songs) and I don't hear it. I do hear a lot of F3's though.
based on Aud tape, cut in Drums is c.30 sec, cut in Around is c.8 sec
Bobby is on fire this whole show. 85 is an extremely strong year for him. this china rider is unreal. bottom is sick.

The first of two nights in Hampton is another great performance from March of '85.  June of this year gets all of the attention but there are several excellent performances from March, including this one, that tend to get overlooked.

The show starts with a rousing Alabama Getaway>Greatest Story that features fiery soloing and solid vocals.  This duo starts the set off with a bang and the energy continues throughout the evening.  They Love Each Other slows the pace a bit but Jerry's vocal performance is good and his solo is very spirited.  An unusual El Paso>Tennessee Jed combo is next, featuring great guitar work by Garcia.  His noodling behind Bobby's vocals during El Paso is very enthusiastic.  Jed is lengthy and twangy, a nice rendition.  The Superstitious/Bottom combo fills the Bobby blues slot nicely, featuring some firey slide work and a nice Brent solo.  The Looks Like Rain>Might As Well combo that finishes the set is enthusiastic and features some great licks from Garcia.

The second set starts off with a bang and continues the energy with an amazing China>Rider which is one of the highlights of the evening.  It starts off a bit sloppy but they pull things together quickly and there is some furious jamming in the transition and during Rider.  Jerry belts out the headlight line and the crowd goes nuts!  A very spacey Playin' concludes the pre Drums segment with a long, dark trippy jam.  This is another highlight of the evening with Boby providing some nice accompaniment to jerry's noodling.  After Space they tease a Playin' reprise but instead go into The Wheel.  A brief Other One has a nice psychedelic jam and quickly segues into a soulful rendition of Wharf Rat in the ballad slot.  The jam at the end is long and intense.  This version should not be missed.  Bob closes out the show with two rockin' tunes.  Don't sleep on this show!

Obviously, we didn't know how special `86 Hampton would be with Phil breaking out "Box of Rain", but in hindsight these 2 shows (esp this night) are largely overlooked. 

Before them, the boys do a solid Cali Feb run and after  these 2, you have Springfield, Nassau, and Philly. For the most part those shows are all 4 stars or better. I KNOW not every show can get 5 stars - kind of defeats the purpose. 

But I agree with 8995 below - Weir is a force in just about '85 show.

I remember people saying "he's trying to hard" or "he wants to be sammy haggar" , etc.... 

IMHO - Weir just steps up for Garcia (whose playing is phenomonal this year, but whose "presence" sometimes wandered). 

Superstious>bottom (did they ever play a bad one?) is unreal here. China>Rider, etc...

Weir could be quirky to some, but he is absolutely "on" for most of the '85 shows. 

This show - in another year - would be in the top 5. But is easy to over look with the aforementioned Spring run...the Summer shows - and of course the legendary Fall East Coast run. 

Enjoy and God Bless.

Good tempo for Alabama>Greatest
Jerry blows lyrics, They would pretty much shelve the getaway after 85, Too bad, I think it is a great tune.
T.L.E.O- Perhaps in a nod to this songs 73 roots they have some zing to this. (Healy with that reverb)
El Paso> Tenn Jed ----85 had a bunch of these odd couplets that worked nicely. 
I Ain't Superstitious ->The Bottom--Notice this keeps the same time as the original MINGLEWOOD from the early days.  "We all need each other, you know its true"
Dupree's Diamond Blues-Song rocked in 85
Looks Like Rain ->Might As Well- The LLR has a faster clip to it. Bob gives us some free advice with a rhyme --- and MIGHT AS WELL is for us dancin' fools!

China ->Rider--Solid. When Jerry was down or scattered vocally, Weir could go up and Garcia's guitar was the center of the GD Universe.
Playing In The Band -> I like the Playin' jam!!!
Drums ->Space ->
The Wheel ->The Other One ->
(They had just done Other 1>Wheel in Berkeley) 
I like the transition from Wheel to Other One which seemed flavored by the pre-drum P.I.T.B jam.
Wharf Rat ->Around And Around ->Johnny B. Goode
(Weir brings the st-stut-stutter for Round)

Good show and i concur with Matthew Vernon
the band is smiling as they play..
Love this spring tour & this start is pretty epic. I mean you have a smoking Alabama Getaway to start, 2nd set great China/Rider & a long jamed out playing.

I can't believe I've never come across this show until today. This is pretty amazing. It starts off with a meltdown version of Alabama>Greatest Story, and doesn't let up. Incredible energy on China/Rider and a fabulous Playin' jam. 

Just when you think things are winding down out of The Wheel, they wind their way into a sick, sick version of The Other One. The intro to this is unique and cool. It starts out as The Other One, and then mutates to where it seems like it could be heading into Truckin' or maybe Satisfaction or some other blues tune before it finally bursts into The Other One. It's a short-ish version, but it's hard to find one with a higher energy level. It's a meltdown.

If there's a downside to this show, it's that Jerry's voice is not in the best shape. It's hard to say how this ranks among all Dead shows, but this one would be perfectly satisfactory on a desert island.

This show always gets me. I was at this show setting front row against the rail on Phils side and before they even get 1/2 way through 'Alabama' I see a glow stick arching through the air and score a direct hit on the side of Phils head. 1st thought was 'asshole' then 'man that had to hurt' then remembered the saying that if Phil is on then its gonna be a great show. I thought that would ruin it for sure. But Phil being the trooper hung in for a great show.  I knock off a star because of lax security of both nights (which is a real shocker of something to bitch about) the next night before the show a guy behind us produced a pistol and  pocket full of ammo. Thats the only time I've narced on someone!

Picking up where they left off after hot the final night at Berkeley.
I fhis isn't. an official release need to happen I don't know what is. Props to this SBD, warts and all, it captures the pure energy of the night nicely.
Alabama>greatest story is on fire! El paso>Jed very cool.  Looks like rain has bobby improve up the wazzo. 
The entire second set is the best playing of the year so far,  stretched out and Great China>Rider, Playing is deeply explorative, love it, long segue into drums and actually we come out of space into a brief reprise post space.  Things somehow swing into a nice wheel and then a mammoth the other one that starts out bluesy if that is possible. Jerry dials up an emotional broken sounding wharf rat from the vocal standpoint.
3rd day job of the year and this song is just not that good....
Bobby is on fire, Brent is really shining, Phil in great form and Jerry's guitar is sizzling at this piont.  Great great show.

reviews.reviewbody: This has always been a fav from 85' but wow, nice SBD!?
Loving this Sugaree.... Jerry soars at around the 4:25 mark.

This show was sometimes traded BITD on a rec for "you gotta check out this Sugaree". Grand indeed, but there are also a couple more highlights. It's an overlooked tour, in the era when Sugaree was peaking and often the best song in the first set. First Set. Jack Straw starts sloppy and with tech problems but then goes overdrive as Jer intently tries to kick things up a notch. Now ready, he wastes not a nanosecond to launch Sugaree. Simply incredible; almost or as good as 9/6 & 11/10 [the SBD is marred by static and the MTX sounds better here]. After a fine Rooster, the second peak of the set is Bird Song. Note @9:55, when Brent starts a melody, how quickly Jer picks it up. The rest is average to below average. Roses is one of just three in '85. Second Set. There are some bright spots in Help>Slip>Franks, along with some sloppiness, blown lyrics and off-beat sections. Either way, there was a high-pitched noise that made it a wash [not from a pedal – that solution would be easy, though it doesn't happen]. Now it can be attenuated with digital filtering, as on the MTX, but it must have been very annoying in person. The noise comes back again during Estimated, but here the MTX is more exciting anyway. Eyes of the World is way uptempo, and it's the back line that bumps it up to respectable. The next section is average '85, until Goin' Down the Road. This is a crisply-ironed, speedway version, and the peak of the set. Keep Your Day Job is in its Sunday clothes, about as good as it got – especially the MTX (though low on Phil). 1st Set:  C 2nd Set: C Overall = 2½ stars Highlights: Sugaree – one of the year's peakers in top form Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad – crisp speedway Keep Your Day Job – if you are looking for a best version SOURCES: Most AUDs run fast. The nak300_barbella-14497 is best. The 150966_sbd_latvala is the updated SBD. It can use some BAL & EQ. The 15403_tetzeli_84410 has a slightly fast second set. The brame_15403 runs at Mickey Mouse speed. The 132153_mtx is the Usborne matrix.

reviews.reviewbody:
The set list is hot, and the Scott Clugston soundboard is rich.
A little short, but sometimes that's just the ticket. Exactly 1 month before the shows released as Dave's 49

fun show with some debuts for the year, tom thumb, shakedown, tons of steel.  Really opening up the catalogue book.
1st set is ok, with odd placement of songs but all competently played.  No real standouts.
Second set elevates the concert for me. They dusted off Shakedown and gave it a good workout. Bobby getting funky on the rhythm, jerry hot on the licks. Kinda odd uncle johns into playing reverse pairing but it all works. Playing goes out there for a while and for the most part works well. Stella is good and Jerry sounds as good as he has vocally during this one. Much better Lovelight then earlier in the year.  two song post space segment is weird.
One of those shows that wont blow you away but also has a lot to offer.

reviews.reviewbody: What a disappointing 2nd set after such a good 1st set!! What's even worse than a 3 tune pre-drums? Looks Like Rain--> Drums!! Always hated LLR in any part of the show, but especially the 2nd set.

Real nice sound..I always return to the1st set on this one like I also do on 4-8-85..cause they are off the HOOK with 2nd sets that are sub par..Truckin'>Smokestack>High time..LOVE IT!! Also special treat with Matthew Kelly playing harmonica on Smokestack..I would like to mention the huge LSD bust in the lot at Nassau during this run..the boys boycotted this venue till the return in the spring of 1990 when you couldn't give a ticket away the 1st night.The band played some monster shows during that run and Nassau became a regular stop again..Lawn Guyland will not disappoint>>>Give it a whirl

reviews.reviewbody: Rejoice! I give five for a reason (or two). This is rare beyond compare. Mid eighties board that does NOT have the keys twice as loud as anything else. Mid eighties board that does NOT have vocals twice as loud as anything else. Mid eighties board with CRISP cymbals. I can't stress this enough. Those with ears know what I mean- the cymbals are NOT wishy washy on this one. Throw in a VERY psyched crowd, a good performance, and a Terrapin 2nd start and PING! TURN IT UP!

Longstrange summed up the sound QUALITY of this board well (don't hear the popping mentioned at all) - fantastic. Strong show - Sugaree, Ramble on Rose, nice rarely heard Ain't Superstitious, smooth Row Jimmy with strong Phil, and a smoking Let it Grow make for a phenomenal 1st set. Terrapin is a nice 2nd set opener & come to think of it could've fit well in that position. Spoonful & Wharf Rat are also hot. Solid night, somebody invent a functioning time machine already!

I wasn't there...no, I was a mere 4-1/2 years old at this point, but I can just imagine during the transition from Throwin' Stones to Sugar Mag seeing Jer look over smiling at Bob who's trying to maintain the Ashes, Ashes while singing to Sugar Mag's tune.  Nicely done as usual.
reviews.reviewtitle: Wish I coulda seen that smile

reviews.reviewbody: past the halfway point of Day Job's short and mostly marginal life.  thankfully.

Bucket>Sugaree
Hell in a Bucket was a tune spoiled by MTV success. It really was a good rocker. Pretty flexible in either set but my preference was somewhere in the 1st set and with Sugaree was probably it's most natural couplet.
This Sugaree-plenty of meat on the bone.-13 minutes
Me &My Uncle>Mexicali-Standard Cowboy tunes 
Ramble on Rose-the boys never seemed to link this up with any other tune, so it stood alone and thus it mainly stayed in the 1st set over the years. Always seemed to get played. i don't remember it ever being shelved.
Jerry gives it a good rendering here.
Bottom>Superstitious-In Hampton they went Superstitious>Bottom kinda cool. Interchangeable 
This didn't get played beyond 1985. 
Row Jimmy-Well Developed
Let It Grow- A Big Kahuna version!
(I prefer this set over set two) 

Set Two
Terrapin -> Women Are Smarter,
 Ship of Fools, 
Truckin'-> Spoonful->
 Drums-> Space
>Wharf Rat->
 Throwing Stones-> Sugar Magnolia,
 E: Day Job

--. Stones>Sugar Magnolia
More jams in the 1st set and predictable Set 2
but I wasn't there & nothing invested here.
So please feel free to differ?
Any antidotes about Downtown Providence,
Brown University Co-eds, Very good blotter etc..
JERRY sounds good vocally & the band is tight!
reviews.reviewtitle: At least I am enjoying the ride.
I was there and experienced my 1st Terrapin
reviews.reviewbody: I attended both nights, but this one was special because it was my first Terrapin.  The ending was explosive but unfortunately I feel you had to be there to understand what I can't put into words. The Sugaree ending of the jam was incredible. Definitely check out the other show.  Providence, RI was a great arena to see the band.

This is likely from the same source as the ciruclating soundboards, but without the apparent Dolby Abuse on the others. Discussing it with the friend I got this from, we think it's no more than 4 or 5 generations.  Obvious care was exercised in handing this down the line... probably nothing but Maxells and Nakamichi cassette decks were used.  It sounds very nice!  Except for:

## --there is a very unfortunate cut in She Belongs to Me at 4:06.56, which lasted for 5.48 seconds.  It appears that someone forgot to "pop the top" off their cassette, so I suspect it's not present on the master (wherever that might be).
--there is some "rolling hiss" at the beginning of Miracle.  Chalk this one up to the ravages of time on cassettes.
** --segments of Drums and Space are obviously missing. The right channel is missing for a few seconds at the beginning of Space. There is a cut between Space and the intro to The Wheel. I have made no attempts at patching these.
--there is no tuning or crowd noise at end of set 1, beginning of set 2 or before the encore. All the songs are there in full, however.



My hope is that this seed will get people to check their cassette collections.  Does anyone have a better version of this?

reviews.reviewbody:
This is a very clear sounding board with a little Matrix sound at just the right times. 

Short show (esp. 1st set, only six tunes) but they make up for it in full focus and wonderful musicianship. 

Phil's "Hi' Ya Kids" mocking Bobby's circa early 70's greeting to audiences is priceless. What a goof-ball! If that wasn't enough a launch into "Why Don't We Do It In The Road" gets the crowd going NUTS. Half Step to follow is ambitious if brief. Bird Song nestled in the middle of 1st set is highlight of the show IMHO. Simply wonderful. Perhaps the best Bird Song of the mid 80s (Placid 83' also comes to mind).

Second set includes "She Belongs To Me" which should make it collector worthy. Women Are Smarter is punchy and agressive, as it should be. Post drums look generic on paper but transitions from Truckin'>Smokestack are polished and seamless. Also, Mydland on Gimmie' Some Lovin' gets really heavy on the B-3 toward the end with wails and howls something crazy making for hilarious interplay. Dew again has Jerry vocally struggling but he brings it through for the climax jam for sure!

Ultimately this won't make it onto the "top ten of 85'" list because there are SO many great 85' performances. This is a short show, and Jerry's voice is shot. But still, playing and energy wise quite at the top of their game. 85' was a majorly up year musically for the band. Way more together than 84' or 86'. Heres a textbook example.

Download this source!
I was a senor in high school and flew out with my tour bros. This set of three shows was the most intense energy I can recall. Bring out the Orb !

this is a long shot..but does anyone have a record of the exact time the Dead were on stage this night? I was born at 8ish pm 04/07/85 on the west coast, making it around 11pm in PA...have always wanted to figure out exactly if the Dead were on stage at the same time, and even try to pinpoint the exact song..
This was Easter Sunday. Heh, heh.

There were only 9 performances of Dylan's "She Belongs To Me" by the Grateful Dead - all in 1985. This was one of the two I heard live that year. I have given all 9 of them a listen, and this is the one I have on my list of Essential Garcia Tracks. 

Why? Froggy voiced Jerry somehow serves the emotional fragility of the storyteller - listen to the 2nd reading of the line "proud to steal her anything she sees" and hear his cracking voice convey exactly how it feels to steal for her.

Before it gets to that line, the first guitar solo @ 1:41 begins to tear down any emotional defenses around me. The 2nd solo @ 3:25 can bring me to tears as Garcia tells a story that can't be related with words. This is one of only 2 or 3 performances which he chose to end not with one last final "paints the daytime black" vocal line, but a fingerpicked run of well placed guitar notes - the way it should be.

I recall more than a few times in 1985 when his voice was shot, a look of frustration crossing the man's face, and when it was time to step back from the mic and let the Tiger do the talking  that expression changed to "I can still do THIS..."

Unfortunately, in this source one channel is phase-inverted, which produces a strange sound. I have corrected this in my DAW and really enjoy the result.
Otherwise a good show.
this is the source you want for this one

Inarguably the greatest six song first set ever, which sounds ridiculous.   So much fun to have the show kick off with Do It In The Road, Phil in rare form.  Not to mention epic versions of Birdsong and Dancin.

And reviewer lpenoza gets it right: a stunning She Belongs to Me, after the Dead resuscitated it after a 19 year absence, a few days earlier in Providence.

The sound is a little off with this one..I saw all three shows this run and this night I was knocking the cobwebs out from the 1st night..Lots of people really love this show and its one for da books~~but I'm sticking with the last night as my personal favorite out of the three..we all have our opinions..Philly is home so I can be a little partial on my rating..but think of all the HOT shows played in the City of Brotherly Shove through the years~~LOTS~!!!!!!! 93.3 FM EST>. in 69'..68' CHRIST.. I SHOULD KNOW THIS~!! well they had FM broadcast of the shows and would really get you pumped to see the boys..I'm ranting~Give It A Whirl~Forever Grateful>Forever Dead~!!

It's an inside joke but, clearly, Phil had seen The Ghoul Show.
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ghoul_Show 
https://youtu.be/t5YOC-Gf8vQ
I remember this wacked-out, low-budge, late-night, 70's-era, horror movie host TV program from my youth in Cleveland.
As far as this show, try this. Drown Jerry out by singing his lyrics as loud as you can and it's a great show.

Short Mississippi 1/2 Step.  Shorter Smokestack Lightning.  The first is unusual, the second seems to be the norm.  I suppose, even though it's a great old Pig tune, there isn't a lot you can do with it.

reviews.reviewbody:
Source says this was (at least in part) patched through by Dan Healy.

I am fairly certain this is the same source I had on my bootleg (but more generations) almost 37 years ago. I played the daylights out of the first set.

I already commented on this show from another source. I think the audience is so crucial to this show b/c the energy level was going to blow off the roof of the Spectrum!!

Tuning: You can hear Bob laying the chords to Midnight Hour, Jerry noodling with Walking the Dog -and I think Phil even does one bass line run of Lovelight. I think the rest of the band was ready before Weir - and Jerry asks him if he "has that thing (guitar) working?? Let's go!"

Then we get the trifecta MH>WTD>BBM...a breather and you hear Phil(?) shout out "Cumberland". Bob obliges with a Me and My Uncle and then we get a blistering "Cumberland" ( I always thought IMHO they should have tagged that to more of Bob's Cowboy tunes.
"Superstitious>Bottom" keeps the horses running full speed. I found that blues number a great break from Bob's Rider,Mingelwood, and Rooster (no disrespect).
Unlike the previous night - this is a long (by '85 standards) first set.

The second set for me is also very good. But more b/c of the post space numbers. GDTRFB>Stella>Round>Lovelight. 

Thanks for this great upload. Enjoy.

God Bless

Unfortunately, in this source one channel is phase-inverted, which produces a strange sound. 
Moreover, it seems like the source was recorded with some Dolby NR, which was not (or not properly) decoded during transfer. It makes the treble sound unnaturally emphasized.
Otherwise a good show.
Different strokes for different folks jam at the 2:34 mark of Midnight Hour . This copy has a lot of hiss though I know it gets better but its tough
I can't decide if this show is exploratory, or just wanders about...

reviews.reviewbody: The only Terrapin > Playing in the Band > Crazy Fingers ever played.  This is also the first time that the three songs appear in the same second set together in any order. The trio has some staying power, but played in the opposite order - CF > PITB > TS

This was one of the best covers they ever pulled off.
I saw this in Philly & entire 1st set was a rocket ride.
(The opener just sent us into orbit.)
It seems to have become fashionable to pile on certain tunes. And for my money anybody smack talking on 85 tunes like WHY DON'T WE DO IT-probably were not at any show(s)(probably still on the tit)
WHY>BERTHA>JACK STRAW- Best opener 85 ?
This is the intensity that i loved about 1985, 
West LA- seems this tune has gained some street credit over the years. Nice to see it Second Set for the 50th anniversary shows. This is Garcia at his introverted  best. A brilliant song for him to explore.
Also good to activate the rhythm section which gets busy throughout this song.
Rooster-Never put this on my fantasy sets but
usually a slide work showcase.
Peggy-O- Very sweet version
As we rolled out to fennario..
Cassidy-Cali Classic
Wheel to the storm and fly
Phil's Bass just right in the mix.
Deal- Primed for lift off!
Danger of flaming out with the quick start out of the gate, but they maintained good forward motion to that DEAL.

Set Two:
Terrapin out of the gate is pretty cool idea.
(Sometimes when they played this later in 2nd set
it seems they could struggle to nail transitions.)
Good to tackle this right up front in the set.
(They opened 2nd set Providence with TERRAPIN.)
Here i really like the progression: TS> Playin>Fingers
Interesting data from KBMILL (first review)
Note: The P.I.T.B- is very trippy, sounds like they might meltdown. For only 10 minutes they take it way out
>Crazy Fingers! at times a challenge for Garcia.
but such a mellow tune. 
Always special when I heard it!
Jerry hums at points here. 
Another sweet jam heading out of Fingers.
A straight ahead traditional Trucking
(no connected Smokestack, Spoonful, High Time)
One super hot jam to end Truckin!!!
Is that like a mini Bird Song jam?
 into Drumz>
The Wheel-> (Can't go wrong with Wheel out of Space)
T.Stones>Sat Night-> E: It's All Over Now Baby Blue
I enjoyed Throwing Stones back in the day. It was Apocalyptic and great spin material but I don't listen to it very often anymore,(it just seems like the Golden Road of the 1980's)
At least they guide it into Saturday Night with a pretty nice Garcia transition briefly raises encore hopes but alas another well traveled Baby Blue is upon us. (Encores NOT a priority for band on most nights in this era.) Still even the last 2 pretty standard tunes sounded just right! EXCELLENT SHOW*****

reviews.reviewbody:
Very nice sound on dis one..You never here people talk about 85' Alpine..why not? This is freakin' HOT..Tons of energy off the gate listen to Bobby & Brent on Waling Blues! Jerry is on fire also! You can hear the crowd going nutz before they break into a nice Althea!
and Brown Eyed Women..Jerry's voice sounds pretty good!! Keep On Growing to open 2nd set!! I caught the one in Merriweather and enjoyed it..should have kept it in the line up..fun song!! 1/2 step is on point and smooth sailing on through..so please>GIVE IT A WHIRL>Forever Grateful>Forever DEAD!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.reviewtitle: I've been mistreated and I don't mind dying

reviews.reviewbody: Half Step > Lost Sailor?

Another Charlie Miller gem...high energy, high speed goodness

(Set II song order is not just exactly perfect)

Hitchhikers halfway across America to see this show !!   It was a wild place to see the dead.. left rhode island with a buddy .. hiked it out there in a week.. lol  did the osley acid and started on night with the Grateful Dead trip the crowd was wild and athene was crazy the scene was crazy lots of love smoke and hugs dancing dancing and more dancing lost sailor was a trip damn is the fantasy just blew me away dear mr. Fantasy and then it was nighttime in the tent with the stars above what a great Grateful Dead show 5 stars in The Sounds beautiful

They go from song to song without much down time between tunes and there is an air of electricity.
Althea almost > Cassidy> all but directly > into B.E.Women
it was a good move to play OMSN as a 1st set closer
(EPIC Pre-Drumz)-
Keep on Growing>Half Step>Sailor >Saint.
The Sailor is a little loose which maybe why they dropped it from the rotation but to me it was pretty important segue into Saint of Circumstance.
FANTASY- building  towards that Red Rocks- Hey Jude!
Miracle out of Mr. Fantasy with Brent slashing away.
I NEED A MIRACLE,,EVERYDAY!

reviews.reviewtitle: TTHIS IS THE LAST TRULY GREAT DEAD SHOW.

reviews.reviewbody: In my experience with Dead shows, they often tailored their sets to the venue, area or weather...and this is a prime example. We drove up to Cincinnati from Lexington,Ky, enjoying a beautiful sunny summer afternoon. Riverbend Ampitheater is set up so you can see the boats behind the stage and are looking across the river into Ky. 1st set the weather was perfect...then the storm clouds built up across the river. A torrential rain storm began during the break, with cloud to ground lightning strikes that made us wonder if the Dead would come back out at all. Of course, they did, during the hardest part of the rain for a scare the bejeezus out of you 2nd set. Enough has been said about the songs themselves, but the circumstances surrounding their performance is what stands out to me. I mean, when they sang "if I had my way, I would tear this whole building down" in Samson, they meant it! It seemed as if they were egging on the storm, daring it to do its worst...thundering drums echoing the actual thunder.And they wanted more. Smokestack Lightning during lightning...I mean come on!!!! Then Cryptical (REALLY?!?!) I remembered the Drums>Space as a frightening experience. WOW!!! You will be hard pressed to find a better show than this, in my opinion. Dick's Picks/Vault are you hearing me?

I wish I could have been peaking about 5' before Iko. But then, judging from my sober state now, why do I feel a bit of the trip in my bones as I listen to this? There is a sound and an edge to this show that is only replicated a few other times. All of them in '85. Several on this tour.
It's so thick that you could rip off chunks.
Yes, trippy as heaven or hell, quite edgy, and one All-Time show. (Is that wretching I hear in the back? You, 100 times, 'This show is an All Timer!' On my desk after you listen to the whole show. Twice.)
I am exhausted after listening to this show. In a good way. A really good way. Like walking out after a great show and you are walking in that wondrous dreamscape. This is a Bobby show, but Jerry, Brent, BK, Micky are there. Lots of dancing around the One. Where's Phil? He shows up once in a while. Maybe he was on Heineken duty. Bobby is manic. The prophet from the burning shore indeed. He does things on this night that he never did again. This is the closest I have heard him play dueling guitars with Garcia for the whole show! And he wins sometimes.

First Set- From Alabama through, it's fun. Closest to not being so is Loser. Maybe Bobby and Healy, who had a so-so night w/ his tricks, threw Jerry off. Bobby proceeds to raffle off they rhythm section as Jerry is beginning the song. Also, Healy throws in space sound, kinda like Asteroids in the day @ 1:36. WTF? Let it Grow is a scorcher and pick of the set. Longest song of the night. Esau and GSET are place and show respectively.

Second Set- This set reminds me of angry sex. A playful beginning and then Here we go! You singing to me? Hot, sweaty, sticky and focused. I have listened to this set maybe more then any other. I received it so long ago and it's transportation music. (Just like another TDIH, hint, hint)
Bobby takes a verse in Iko for the only time. Listen to Brent in here. You wouldn't notice too much if you didn't pay attention, but he is right there to fill or nudge at the right times. Where is Healy @ 7:30 w/ Garcia's mike? Bad Healy. Too many mistakes this night that are too boring to recount, but he has his moments of redemption.
Samson is a beast. Just a reminder that this needs to played Loud. What an into! When it hits @:42 it's a Maxell guy in the chair moment. If the first set was good times, we are having great times now. Finger snapping, bopping along GD! Yeah! One of my fav. Samson's. Bobby. Bobby. Bobby.
And then things turn dark in tone. O.K. kiddies, you had two songs to dance to. He's Gone is mournful. Listen for Bobby in this one. What a tone and 'aint backing down. Everyone is where they are supposed to be. A beautiful and short version. Because around 7:30 Smokestack begins to slither into the song.
And what a Smokestack! O.K. gauntlet thrown down. This is the Best Bobby Smokestack bar none. An incredible intro, same with vocals. Conjuring the voodoo.
Why did they bring back Cryptical? The intro is 1:48, the outro :41. Shortest new song they could revive? I can understand him not wanting to sing it, but it's a great song to play.
Drums would have me bopping but nothing beyond the pale.
That can not be said of Insectiod Space, which begins the last two minutes of Drums. You know drums is over by the screaming.
Space we pass by 98% (a guess) of the time. I wouldn't miss this one. Unless you have just taken a bunch of hallucinogens and are having a bad time of it. Dark and creepy with many a TOO tease, a train whistle, and mooing cows. And the insects. All through, Jerry provides a quiet little place, so if you get scared you can run to Jerry. When Phil comes back it's full on TOO teasing and then,
Jerry drops in one of the most beautiful Comes A Time. This song is one that is better, later. This is a CAT for Jerry freaks like Arb. and Ring. As Grisman said (in general about Garcia), there is a high emotional content to this song. His solo is most beautiful and nestles into your heart or rips it out. "Only love can feel."
Remember the loud reminder? Well, we are into TOO territory. It suffers a bit from not having the momentum of Space, but recovers quickly. Hey, there's Phil! It takes 1:30 for them to find each other and then here we go! Short, intense and a lead into Jerry's biggie of the night.
This Wharf Rat is titanic. I don't care about flaws or whatever. The band gives its all for this song as you can tell by how tired they sound at the end of the set. Jerry's tone again starts out weary, but filled w/ desperation. Those little spoken words, dropped so quietly. I can't recall , "some other fuckers crime", sounding so clear. Then the gospel portion is beautiful. Not much jamming here, but what there is, fits right in. Bobby trying to go at it with Garcia at the end.
R & R- Is surprisingly decent. Maybe even good. Well, lets not get crazy. Brent finally takes his first (and short) solo of the night.
GLove- Tired, tired GD. Not a song I like anyways. An interesting rap by Bobby @ 5:08. Prescient? Or the more things change, the more they stay the same?
USB Rocks! Jerry and Bobby go at it again one more time.

edit- I love this quote from Evan S. Hunt, "What a hideously sick and raunchy version of USB this is. Sloppy> mistakes> galore> ignore> brilliance. All that change all that fast. A presence that follows you around and gives you chase to rhythm." 1985 in a nutshell.

What a tremendous performance. Bravo!
Great recording of a killer show. The lightning going off over the river during Let it Grow and the sky during Cryptical sent this one way over for me!

reviews.reviewbody:
This is my favorite recording of the show
the others have a hiss that appears and goes away very quickly but it is piercing and comes back again
this recording also keeps the energy feeling

5 star show (yet to find a non 5 star show;))

Major Highlights off the top of my head:
day tripper opener
Row Jimmy (A+)
Me n my Uncle
Jack Straw
Gimme some Lovin'
Touch Encore: Song always brings hope
The Playin' is where the magic is at, something about it always brings me back...beautiful chaos and Jerry is just going off, he has something to say and is saying it. Brent and drummers also have a little melt at the end
very scary space and a very eerie china doll
while you are here check out the playin'
might as well?(~);}

If anyone has the second set on tape i'm willing to trade
I have the first set but not the second!
Love the mid-1980s Sugar Mags, and this is a corker... nice long jam pre-SSDD, unstoppable crashing rhythm, they are a machine chewing up everything before them!

reviews.reviewtitle: giant cricket sucked my brain through 3rd eye socket
Wow. Definitely worth hearing twice!!! Or more!!!
reviews.reviewbody:
This show reminds me of my very first Dead show at the Omni in Atlanta in '87 & exactly why I dearly LOVE the music the Grateful Dead created in concert. it is unmistakable. So beautiful that you feel like your soul is dancing and soaring high above your body.!! In between '87 & ''95 I was able to see Grateful Dead a little more than 70 times.. Unfortunately I never got to see them at Merriweather Pavillion although I have seen a number of shows there. I'm sure most everyone there had a great time. I moved from Atlanta to the DC area in '93. When they tore down the Omni to make way for the Olympics I almost cried!! I saw my very first concert there when I was in the 6th grade. ACDC in 1979. And went on to see more shows there that I can't remember them all. I'd have to make a list. Same with the Pavillion in Gainesville, VA. It was Nissan Pavillion at first. Now it's JiffyLube Live. 
☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆
Ok, Review. I don't really like comparing different versions of songs. Different "eras" have different versions of some of the same songs. I don't like doing it or saying it but April 1st, 1990 at the Omni the encore is "It's All Over Now Baby Blue." I never really liked that version. My brother loved it but it just idk didn't do it for me. Because of THAT I almost skipped the version here. But OMG!!! The version here is so so much better to my ears!!! It's never been one of my favorites anyway but JERRY really does a great job & actually MAKES ME LIKE THIS SONG when b4 I had just kinda tolerated. 
Review☆☆☆☆☆☆ They open with "Dancin in the Streets" and this isn't the Cornell 77 marathon Dancin with the cool guitar effects but I personally like it more cuz it's not so long that it gets boring. But that guitar special effect does shoe up in "Dupree's Diamond Blues" & it works well for it & they do a very solid rendition. "Walkin Blues" is next & this is probably the best version of it I've ever heard although I'll admit I haven't listened to a lot of early 80's YET. After hearing this gem I'll be fishin for sure! "Jack-a-Roe" is frickin awesome!  I've always loved this tune & Jerry doesn't disappoint even for a second. Then comes "My Brother Esau" & "Stagger Lee" & both are solid & fun AND things really pick up speed with "Let it Grow" & at first I thought they would close the set with it but Jer decided to put a"Keep Your Day Job" in for good measure 
I☆★☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆♡♡♡♡♡♡♡♡
Second Set- Scarlet/Fire, Playin> Uncle John's Band, While the Scarlet Begonias & Fire on the Mountain are both good separately but the "weave" from one to the other just isn't there. Which kinda surprised/disappointed me. But the "Playin" gets REALLY GOOD!!! Jerry throws down.  Well everyone throws down!!And Uncle J's is OK. 

I'll have to finish later.

reviews.reviewbody: I don't know why anyone would call this the worst show ever. It's a good show.

Charlie beat me to the punch...I have heard those same words about this show.  I have been pumping this particular Stranger->China-> Rider through my speakers since I was like 16 or 17 years old-so soooo wish I was on a ski lift in the middle of the summer up to Grateful Dead peak in the summer of '85. My experience has always been a low gen. audience-as ALWAYS  I am very very psyched to have a Miller delivery of another solid board!

I wasnt there, I saw Alpine through Ventura, but I always thought this show got a bad rap.  Is it the Fix or Greek or second night Richmond or 4.7?  No.  Worst show ever? No. I thought 4.6 first night Philly was worse. I know a couple of people who went and anything negative I heard from them was more about the venue, not the show itself, i.e. the dust, the traffic, one road, etc.  Which were perhaps valid since everyone said the same thing and the band never went back.

A must-stream from a great, well-played and consistent ytear.  Thanks to Charlkie for his fantastic ear and efforts, all us mid-'80's Heads appreciate it very much.

the he's gone >>truckin' says it all...they were off this night, even if there were a few bright moments, they can't save this stinker...

i'm off to some '68 land now...

mixed well, always a fan of Alabama Getaway as a opener 
typical 85 sound band is fast, jerr is slow. 

lacks JG's engery
The person usuing the screen name Charlie Miller is not the same C Miller that remasters these shows. His screen name is skb archives because he is the archivist for The Steve Kimmock Band.
Good show. Nice sound.

This show was terrible. The sound from the tapes don't tell the true story. It was blazing hot. About 98℉. Dusty and the sound system never got 'dialed in'. Bobby kicked his amp so hard it flew across the stage! Show started in the middle of the afternoon and was finished before darkness set in. Just a weird day all around.

Wow...that Day Tripper performance is something else. I don't think I've ever heard them sound more out of steam and out of sync with each other than that performance. What's going on with the drums?! Sounds like they couldn't get out of that rolling loops :(

I had a ticket for this show. Decided on not going, cuz I had transportation issues. After reading accounts of this show, glad I didn't. Therefore, as a result of my accidnental intuition, I hereby give myself 5 stars!
reviews.reviewtitle: Sometimes, it pays not to go!

reviews.reviewbody:
Yeah it was a weird couple of days... Most of the local shops restaurants ran out of food/supplies by the day of the show. A buddy of mine were low on funds and eating at a local place, the coolest waitperson gave us a huge plate of fries to share. Never forget that...
Yeah Bobby was kicking the heck out of his amp... What was more impressive though, he was wearing a super thin set of sneakers, dang tuff feat from all that running I guess!!    
It was a hot weird day, so-so show but nothing but good memories for me!!
30 years ago today. Not every Dead show was a bowl of cherries. I dig this shows Minglewood, FOTD, West L.A. and Stranger. Any show with Jerry and Brent is good enough for me.

I drove up the mountain and camped on the back side, bedded down at dark - probably 10. Woke to all the travelers everywhere who had drove through the night to get there from the desert. The local store was foraged over and empty. It was a rushed show at a high altitude in the brutal heat. Friend of the Devil was magic and I stayed the night in Reno. The attitude of the crowd was great, fun show.

This was a landmark show for me for many reasons.  Touted as the highest Dead show ever, it was nice to be backstage.  139 years prior, my forebears spent the winter nearby in what is known as the Donner Party.  Patrick Breen Jr is my second great grandfather; his father kept the now famous diary.  

We drove up from SF to Truckee, staying at Nurse Barbie's which was quite the social gathering in and of itself.  

I came back to this location (roughly) 11 years later in 1996 to deliver the key note speech to the crowd gathered for the Donner Party's sesquicentennial, reading the lyrics to Big Head Todd's Monument in Green.  

As for the show, I have fond memories.  There were technical difficulties and it was bloody hot. But I'm glad I was there among so many friends.

Like one other reviewer, it was hot, no shade (ski slope), dry, dusty, Hot August tells it all. It's also at 7700 feet, so some of us not used to walking miles really suffered. 

They never got tuning right, seems they spent more time in first half set tuning, until bobby kicked his unit, I think they played another song, and took a break until the sound got somewhat better.

Meanwhile in the hot sun. 

Finished the first set. 
Second set wasn't bad. Stranger was the only song I didn't have on my first tape. Didn't know it was day tripper until halfway though the verse, ugh as I remember.

Another fat sounding '85 show.  The recording lacks the bass that many others from '85 have, but the music here is for the most part what we craved then and now.  If you ain't been there, now is as good a time as any.

This is by far the best source so far.  The pitch on the other boards is messed up, and the matrix is kind of swirly and though it masterfully corrects the pitch, it still has some sonic issues.  I am sure it was a near impossible task with this show & the sources available, but the bait of the set list and the allure of '85...?  Hard to resist huh Mr. Seamons?
well, they certainly made up for a weak first half of the second set, didn't they?

reviews.reviewbody: The start of the 6th (of 7) Red Rocks runs and 4th year in a row. The shows were changed to the afternoon after tix were printed, because at the time there was an attempt to appease the people in the nearby exurban enclave of Morrison, after a Shakedown appeared on their Main Street in '84 (the afternoon showers are over by September). Saturday started in the evening anyway. At the Greeks, a couple months earlier, Cryptical was surprisingly resurrected, and paired with Other One for the first time in over 13 yrs. They busted it out 4 more times, so of course many of us thought there would be a Cryptical for this run, and there was a bzz bzz bzz about this being the final one. By the time this run was over, we didn't get one! The show before, in KC, turned out to be the last. They did add Revolutionary Hamstrung shortly after (but dropped it immediately), and Tons of Steel had just been added, too. First Set. An above-average Cold Rain bodes well. There's a He's Gone tuning but they veer instead into See See Rider. I'd missed it every time and finally got to see one. (I still kept oddly missing Alabama, and missed TLEO and Might as Well until the 90s!). Luckily this was the one to see; though there's a mixing problem the performance is tops (Bobby doesn't abuse his slide privileges). Candyman sounded bad on my old AUD but now I can see how great it was. The Beat it on Down-9 is average and the next few are creaky and/or sluggish until a whopper of a Me & My Uncle fires the band. Now there's a boogie in the air for Big River where Brent is given room. Peggy-O is spry and bouncy for the era and I love the solo on this one. Jer then asks for Black Muddy (wtf?!). Let it Grow improves but the band isn't tight. The AUD I had for years and years was wobbly here, but the SBD shows it's a good version, sans Bobby straining for the early verses. It's a short set (fwiw, the shortest set I ever saw - not counting 3-set shows). Second Set. So, this Scarlet is in my Top 5 of all time. I still remember thinking, when Jer played it, that I would have to get the tape to make sure I heard what I thought. I still can't get over the unusual way Garcia transposes several times during the solo, plays one phrase and then several measures later plays the phrasing in reverse (which I discovered when I worked it out on the fretboard), and figures out a way - on the fly- to have several peaks, including a fanfare section near the end and an ascending finish that goes unresolved, accelerating before returning to verse. The tranny into the hot Fire is also amazing. Bobby flubs an otherwise good Estimated Prophet. Eyes is Motorik and Jer is on-game. Drums is a great headphone version and in my Top 20 of all time. They had a new Line Array tower at these shows and I remember how knock-your-sox powerful it was for Gimme Some Lovin'. After a Sugar Mag sweet clover daydream, they feel out whether that's really it or not (though it was normally the set-ender in '85) but, waters tested, somebody bails. Brokedown has the best false start that I know of (it was the talk of Shakedown after the show), then they come back and nail the harmony. 1st Set:  B- 2nd Set: B+ Overall = 4 Stars Highlights: See, See Rider Blues - best of the 15 in '85 Me & My Uncle - maybe best of '85 Scarlet Begonias - maybe it's just me, but one of all-time best Eyes of the World - Jer is on-game and the '85 beat Motorik Drums - unusually good, a head-game off the sandstone; try headphones SOURCES: There haven't been great sources for this show, with dragging SBDs and swimmy, static-y, saturated AUDS dominating (though it was still a repeat-listen for me for years). But now there's a much-improved, correctly pitched and patched SBD [tobin_102034], and a great matrix [tobin_102032].

reviews.reviewbody: multiple cuts in this source-these were all great shows, Weir climbed the scaffolding during Sugar Mag and continued to play far above the stage
The only cut is during the tape flip in space.
Brent snuck a Never Trust a Woman in on us there.  The first in 15 months and a song that was rarely played in 84, 85 and 86 before a moderate resurgence.

I love this era of the Dead because Jerry was playing so damn great so much of the time. 85 has its issues but when it comes together it's fantastic.

This show took me by surprise. It's got confidence and creativity and energy and I highly recommend it to fans of this era.

The only caveat is the Never Trust A Woman which has to be up there on the leaderboard of all time Dead train wrecks. Jerry leaves the stage after Eyes (not uncommon at this point) and Brent starts the tune but the drummers aren't having it. There's a jarring musical tug of war, then a jam at the drummers' tempo, then eventually they cave and play the song. It's messed up but if you love these guys you will find it interesting at least.

1) At the beginning of the show,  39.388 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the video.

2) Between Bertha and It's All Over Now, 1 minute and 21.581 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the video.

3) Between It's All Over Now and Row Jimmy, 21.519 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the video.

4) Between Row Jimmy and My Brother Esau, 1 minute and 17.389 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the video.

5) Between Big RailRoad Blues and Looks Like Rain, 04.455 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the video.

6) About 1 minute into Help On The Way, .136 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the audience.

7) 8 minutes into Franklin's Tower, .120 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the video.

8) Between Franklin's Tower and Playing In The Band, 7.786 seconds was repeated on the soundboard audio and was deleted in order to match the video audio.

9) At the start of Space, 23.482 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the video.

10) At the end of NFA Chant, 49.668 seconds were missing from the soundboard and was filled using audio from the audience.

11)  Matrix\DTS and Soundboard were synced using the video as a timing reference until the end of Black Peter (when the video was cut) afterwhich the audience was used as it was more consistent.

12) NOTE: The Darby Audience came in 24/48 format and the Soundboard came as 16/44 format. Using R8brain Pro, the Soundboard was expanded to 24/48. After matrix was mixed and soundboard was patched, R8Brain Pro was used to reduce matrix and soundboard to cd compatible 16/44.

Brokedown House Production

reviews.reviewbody:
... over under around and through the spurious machinations of mixerman Healy's first set experiments with brand new effects toys, then one might consider this concert to be a true voyage into the the land of the curious.

For some reason, the second set is not beset with these P.A. anomalies and things turn into normal -- normal, that is, for the Dead in those days. 

1985 wasn't a half bad year for the band and this show is certainly exemplirary of that premise.

The playing is a little rushed and sloppy at times but all in all it's right on the money. Jerry lets it fly as often as not and curries an acceptable favor. 

What really makes this show and why it is so resplendent with groove bags is because of Phil's playing and the recording of the bass is just as I like it, anyway -- very present and very articulated. When Phil is on such as he is on in this particular capturing, then you know the band is in synch that night.

Kudos to Kevin Tobin who really knows his stuff around the re-presentation of these sundrious recordings and versions of recordings. You know that when you read of his name ascribed to one of these deals then you know that it's going to be good.
reviews.reviewtitle: If One Can Wend One's Way...

reviews.reviewbody: ... through 1st set (thanks for tips, previous reviewer!) and began w/HSF (in Playin' now), but agreed that "the bass player" sounds fantastic.  The howling and shrieking sound throughout is kinda weird, but easily forgiven, considering clarity, separation and spunk.  Thanks to all involved (especially Tobin) for terrific quality in rendering these files.
after a lot of experimentation earlier in the year, this run of shows features more set lists that are similar to the early Brent years.

reviews.reviewbody: Solid but average show. Highlights are bluesy JG solos and nice BW rhythm during a great 1st set Smokestack Lightnin.
Average show.The 2nd set was a little strange?Love the She Belongs To Me from this show!!

I think the show is better than the other reviews have said.  That's a hot Scarlet > Fire, and the Twilight Tuning prior to it was great.  Very unusual setlist, LONG pre-drums, strangely-placed and highly energetic US Blues, and another great '85 Drums/Space... I like this one very much indeed.  Jerry messes up verses on Comes A Time, but hey, he's got to blow SOME lyrics at just about every show, so I'm cool with it :)

this show is a very underrated show i first heard the She Belongs To Me on a friends Frost show the year before as a filler just listened to it in full last night was a rockin show well played too imo very solid Smokestack one of the best since the early 70's above mentioned She Belongs To Me too was a personal favorite of mine and rocked Comes A Time another killer song played well the Dupree's is also played well all in all sound quality a 5 show wise 4.5 hate to go with a 5 so i'll give it a 4

Gets the rare 4 1/2-HG (4 & 1/2 stars-hidden gem). The Sep '85 focus seems to be on the Red Rocks shows, which are great, or the Kaisers, overlooking one of 85's Top 5 shows - better than Dick's 21, Merri-Post or the New Year's run; maybe better than 11/10/85, and a few other standards. The First Set is only 45 minutes but the Second is an hour longer! Devore is a community college. One of the only times I bought an official T-shirt (they didn't used to cost $30, kids!), I wore this date on the back (but took forever to hear the show) and I recall we briefly considered going to this show and skipping the Kaisers after Red Rocks. Ah well, the Rocks run satiated. First Set. The sound is still being leveled for Alabama ("rope enough to burn himself" and Jer forgets 23rd Psalm but starts hot enough). Except for a shaky Dupree's, the rest of the set is above average. West LA has a roaring solo, Jer starts a tornado in Mama Tried. Bobby miscues Big River but the final solo is x-factor-whopper. They only did a 1st set Smokestack twice in 85. Deal is excellent. Second Set. The Twilight Zone tuning was from the era when Merl Saunders was the musical director for the 80s TV version (the full Dead Twilight Zone album was released in' 98 - the worst product to carry the Dead name). It's too bad they didn't use the taped effects segue all month. This and 9/5 are perhaps the two best Scarlets of 85. Phil and Brent are hot and Fire is up there with 5/7/77, 12/30/79, 10/14/80, & 10/14/83. Same for Samson - unbelievable, jawdropping soloing! She Belongs to Me is the 6th of 9 times, all in 85, and probably the best. Truckin' is concisely played and very active - Garcia tight as fukk and Bobby flubs only one line! Comes a Time has an amazing solo and great Brent. Around comes before Drums. I don't know how much this happened overall but it only happened once in the mid 80s. It's a sudden drop-in from Jer with Bobby immediately adding non-standard echoey fills. The US Blues/Satisfaction pairing is a peak blowout. There were 8 of the latter in 84-86 and this may be best. 1st Set:  B- 2nd Set: A+ Overall = 4½ Stars Highlights: Deal - Listen to what Bobby weaves behind Jer's 1st solo Whole 2nd set - (sans the encore - it's a wash). There are several jawdropping sequences/pairings, particularly Scarlet>>Truckin' & Space>>Satisfaction. SOURCES: Definitely the miller.34722. She Belongs to Me is on Postcards.
My friend made the arrangements for the Dead to play Devord Field at Southwestern College in Chula Vista and we got backstage. Excellent sound quality! Thank you!

...are for unfortunate children who are still subjected to an archaic rating system, not the Grateful Dead. The Satisfactory/No Credit option offered at Brown University trumps traditionalism and is the only grade or star that should be applied to this overachieving band. They are always. at the least, "satisfactory." So, take your grades and stars back to your inferior public school where they belong. They have no place here.

The show was like a bonus show. It went on sale after the rest of the tour did. The second set was the the best I ever saw, they almost forgot to play drum/space. The Scarlet-Fire was an out of body experience for me. Totally awesome.
there's more to this than certainly meets the eye, and even though it doesn't seem like an outrageous monster of a show, I can't help but dip back into the sound.

reviews.reviewbody:
The Source, and Notes could have been clearer:  Set 1 is a FOB AUD, and I'd give it one star. It's unbalanced: too much cymbals and other high-end sounds.,it also has drop outs, clicks, and the levels get turned up too high initially.  I couldn't listen to it.

Set2 is a SBD, and I'd give it a 5 for quality, but the Dew has quriky tempo and lacks Umph.  I give the performance a 3.

The"DEAL" opener is an AUD. recording, the rest of the show is a SUPER SOUNDING SBD!! erik64 or 65, who ever you are, you didn"t listen to the whole 1st set! I got a flashback buzz listening to this show, and I wasn't even there! Some sloppiness from the band at times, but so what! They rock and this recording rocks! Great mid-80's sound! Thank you Mr.Charlie!! Thanks for the heads up Burnt Rich!!!
reviews.reviewtitle: erik65 You rushed your vote! This SBD gave me a flashback! Uncle Charlie strikes again!

reviews.reviewbody: Iceman, in YOUR rush to comment, you over looked it is Deal opening up the show, not Bertha.  ;)

How often did that happen. 1st set is "backward" too, with a  Deal opener.
 Its a long 2-lane road to the sportatorium.Stuck in bad traffic after workin the delivery van, my brother who was not a deadhead told me to go on and walk if I wanted to catch the beginning of the show, and we would meet at the set break. I looked and looked until the boys came back on stage and dropped into the Dew....
After the show my bro was out in front of the show drunk assed in the van--He went to the DOG TRACK!
reviews.reviewtitle: Dude, its a 2nd set Dew opener.

reviews.reviewbody: The boys were in a HUGE rush on this show...........Slow Down!  Drugs are still going to be there fellas...hated the "80's  Thank;s Charlie!!!!
I would have guessed it was opposite day had the encore not been Baby Blue

So you came for the 1st set Deal opener hope you rode it thru to the Let It Grow closer,
So you come for the 2nd set Morning Dew opener hope you made it thru to the Eyes>Drums>Space>Miracle.
1985 was the year for me (touring 84>93)
Give me a rocket charged freight train --1985
For This Year --a 2nd tier sugary goodness.           Strong 4 bolts!
Old Sportatorium-nuff said.
One of those rare nights in the mid 80's 
when Garcia has more to offer vocally than Weir.
and what a pretty EYES OF THE WORLD.
Deal is not my favorite anyway. I leave it off my recordings.
Brent helps out on backup vocals on It’s All Over Now. Loser and Let it Grow are solid.

reviews.reviewtitle: Yet another hot show from a great run
reviews.reviewbody:
I'm a fan of the October/November 1985 east coast tour. The band was cooking - songs were typically high tempo and full of energy. Both Bobby and Jerry were generally in good voice throughout this run, certainly by their mid 80s vocal standards. The November 1st date in Richmond was immortalized as Dick's Picks Volume 21, followed by a 2nd night in Richmond that could just as easily have been made an official release, and the Halloween show in Columbia, SC is another fan favorite that opened with a unique Space > Werewolves Of London. 

This night's first set has a high energy start, with the band zipping through Alabama Getaway and Promised Land. Another highlight is a smoky West L.A. Fadeaway with Jerry locking into a groove in the solos. Jerry adds some interesting riffs to this version of Minglewood, which also features a hot solo from Brent. Overall this isn't my favorite selection of 1st set tunes from this era, but I have no complaints regarding the performances.

The 2nd set is where this show really lifts off. A hot China > Rider pairing kicks things off after the intermission, followed by inspired versions of PITB and Terrapin Station, both featuring nice jam sections. 80s versions of Playing typically aren't selected by fans to be among the best versions of the song, which is understandable if you compare them to the towering performances from the Keith and Donna lineup, but Playin' frequently featured some of the best pure improvisation from the Brent era. The Wheel emerges out of a weird and interesting Drums/Space, followed by a sprint through Truckin', a powerful Wharf Rat performance, and celebratory versions of Sugar Magnolia and US Blues (Bobby signs off with: "thank y'all, see ya mañana") -- but strangely US Blues is missing from this source.

This a nice sounding source, which has a bit more clarity, separation, and high end detail compared to the other SBDs, at least to my ears. The lack of the encore US Blues is an odd omission, but my recommendation is to listen to this source for the rest of the show and switch to one of the other SBDs to hear the encore. 

Maybe I'm being overly picky by giving this show "only" 4 stars, because again, the performances in set 1 are perfectly fine, but during the whole stretch from Minglewood through Might As Well I just get impatient wanting to get to the much more interesting 2nd set. On the whole this is a good representation of the Dead in fine form in the mid 80s, and is a recommended listen if you want to dig deeper into this era beyond the lauded Nov 1st Dick's Picks show.

reviews.reviewbody:
It was complete pandemonium as the ticketless Heads surged the turnstiles and by the 2nd set the Byrne was over capacity.
A wild show and my tamborine got passed around the arena during Cassidy.

THE BEAUTIFUL ROSE
I can tell that you have travelled this road 
not by the footprints
 but from the roses

I can tell by your smile
you like your roses wild
That rose in your hair just tickling your ears

The love of my life 
Beauty of my World
The love of my life is a rose

She got thorns i respect
Places i just can't touch
Like the first buds of Spring
Do you know what joy you bring.

From Sadness , To Pleasure
Life's sacred treasure
The flowers at Heaven's door

And when in bloom 
there is nothing more fair
The Love of my life is a rose

-Chris Freedom

Thank you to my sister Mary Ann and Michael for lodging
us for the show. So memorable and such a great tape.
Woo Hoo!!

reviews.reviewtitle: Sing of death and loss oh Grateful Dead Muse!
reviews.reviewbody: One of the great Jack Straws they did between the fall of 84 and the spring of 86 lands us into the desert with this stark depiction.  I really like the soundboard the best for this set.  It’s a clean one to thx Charlie Miller!  It allows you to hear the subtleties like Jerry’s final nail in the coffin for poor old Shannon when he sings ‘laid his body down’ in a rebuking tone as if to quickly say “told you so” .  His lead, when it finally finds its way to the mix is fiery and intense.  Peggy-O is spirited and darkly celebratory.   High Time is the showstopper, the most overlooked version and possibly the best version of the year.   I love shows with BIODTL.  That’s the real deal there.   I have to say I’m surprised at the energy of this show b/c our impression of this run on the east coast was reserved only to the second set of the night they played She Belongs to Me which I always considered to be a sleepy set weighed down by tryptophan or some kind of trypo, crypto-something.   Not this one though: three rockers in a row to end the set.  Back in a bit.  Second set opens with what’s probably a continuation of the argument from the first set between Bobby and the drummers except here it sounds a little bit serious and I wonder if that energy will spill over.  It sounds like Bob is not ready and Phil is late.  Oh well.  So they play a song about saying shove it you know where.  I love the 85 Aikos (yeah, east coast) b/c they’re peppy and not as stretched out as they would later get.  84-86 is the heyday imo.  This is a good one , goes along at a clip and has a big confetti rave up at the end.  At this point in things, you’re wondering if Aiko means you’re going to get one of those brisk Estimated>something into drums but it’s Lost Sailor which is getting rare though you don’t know it and that holds promise of another Jerry song before drums.  It’s Terrapin which leads to a chaotic, primal jam and Don’t Need Love.  Is it the first one Jerry plays on? Perhaps.  The post drums has a sweet Stella Blue and an over-the-top Sugar Magnolia that Jerry does about half a minute of scrubbing to close the main section.  U.S. Blues continues the rockin’ theme.

reviews.reviewbody: So here we are - Last night was so satisfying, it could have been a one show run - but I got walked into this show by Steve Marcus, right through the front door of the Kaiser on a rainy night in November with nothing but the shirt on my back and a smile on my face - Willy caught my eye as Steve held open the side door, as if to say, "Whoever you are, boy, have a great time, 'cause you're lucky as hell..." - with a pass slapped to my shirt and no stub in my pocket, I headed to the backstage bar to get a beer- and got caught standing in line when Bob first broke with the BBP - undaunted, I abandoned my quest for alcohol and slithered from the side curtain into a position pressed against the wall in front of Phil - slowly but surely to spend the rest of the set maneuvering my way into the center front for this exceptional event -  The Kaiser was one of those great venues that the Dead played in the 80's, along with the Greek and the Frost, where no matter where you found yourself, it was a great place to be - both figuratively and  metaphorically - This show is my top ONE - best I ever saw - and that's out of more that 100 - I've listened to this recording many, many times to confirm this status, and have yet to be dissuaded -  The second set is as they say, "seamless" - in this case this refers to not only the recording but the performance - listen to the very last guitar notes before drums, as Jerry lets you know that they will return with Other One after a smoke and a drink - this is the peak of the 80's, by this reviewer's measure, and I'm proud to share it with you...

I remember when got the tapes of this show from my west coast connection...SOOO HAPPY! A very fun show with a nice start with the Big Boy Pete..I started going to shows in the early 80's so I can be partial to the Brent era..85' was such a fun year with some exciting well played shows..even if Jerry's voice was off at times!! I love the job Healy did at the mixing board in 85'.. Most of the soundboards are superb and this is one off them. A solid show from start to finish...Give it a whirl

My only gripe about this show is it sounds like Jerry smoked an entire carton of cigarettes before the concert. The setlist of this show is what makes it a winner. "Big Boy Pete" is a wonderful surprise 25 years after it was played last. "She Belongs to Me" is beautiful. "Walking the Dog" encore? This show is special from start to finish. Five stars for the setlist, the performance, and of course, the beautiful CM transfer. Amazing for 1985 or any year. A keeper for sure.
Wow WTF Wow that's all Just Freakin Wow more stars than you can see Just Wow Jerry Garcia Wow

A good show with great sound.
I like Garcia's tune selection from start to finish.
Yes, Jerry has the raspy voice but not a Fisherman's Friend emergency by any means.
They give him the Chula Vista cruiser here and there like in Might as Well.
First set is HOT!
The 2nd set is even more amped up.
the Shakedown>Crazy Fingers (strange but cool bedfellows for 1985)
 Of special note is the P.I.T.B which starts mid-set. The jam here brings back happy memories of the early 70's.
Jerry goes for SHE BELONGS TO ME and to me that was one of the best ballads of 85. 
Other1>Wharf Rat>Playing reprise>Gimme Some Lovin>Midnight Hour
Very generous and very wide open. The Playing reprise just flows! Both GIMME and MIDNIGHT HOUR are great!!!Phil goes "Going to kick ass, like everybody should"
e) Walking the Dog This is very sharp, the Dead are crisp and grooving, The version I heard on the East Coast did not have half the mojo this one does.
I bumped this up to a 5 because it is an outstanding show with great sound with excellent tune selection and well played!!!
brilliant first half of the second set

reviews.reviewbody: Decent "Off Air" recording. The boys come out and appear to feed off the crowd and launch into NFA instead of TOG! High energy show!
Bobby is a little chatty in this one - maybe because it is a radio broadcast.  Great sound matrix.  Nice CC Rider, LIG and double encore.
Sounds like Father Guido Sarducci!  (I don't know how to spell that).

I will grant you - that there are other Nye shows that are longer than this and (I guess for some people) stronger b/c of that.

Another complaint I remember at the time was that the boys did not do a 3rd set.

But what I notice when I listen to this (again after 26 years) was the same thing I noticed when taping it back then: the electricity between the crowd and the boys.

Set one is solid with a NFA opener (even when commentator says..."sounds like nfa to me."). The segue into touch was awesome b/c while the boys had been playing touch for some time, it was not "burned out". The rest of the set is above average. Nothing really out of the ordinairy - but solid play, just as they had done at most of their shows in '85.

The midnight hour>Sugaree really was awesome. It is easy in retrospect to look back and wonder "why not break out St. Stephen or Dark Star? But the thing is the boys had revived many tunes in '85 including crazy fingers, cryptical big boy pete, big boss man, kansas city, baby what you want me to do. I know that is not an exhaustive list. 
The playing is stellar after that women>ship>playin>terrapintruckin>blackpeter>throwinstones>nfa>nfa reprise> lovelight//brokedown.
Very solid show and one that I think deserves more credit than some are giving it. 

God Bless and Enjoy!
