reviews.reviewbody: Good recording, but the band is not at their best.
not a big fan of 80s dead sound quality isnt bad tho

Maybe not one of their best performances, but the Women>Aiko>Women is certainly historic.  I've been wondering for twenty years why they never did a medley of these two songs -- which are musically virtually identical.  Well, they did, and here it is!  So at least grab these three tracks and check 'em out.

not a big fan of 80s Dead, what else is there?
other than a couple isolated years in the 70s and a few brief moments of greatness in the late 60s, it's slim pickens...  oh, right, you like Phish, that explains a lot. :-)

while you wouldn't know it judging by these Oakland shows, summer and fall '85 is where it's at if you can get away from your Keith/Donna tapes long enough.
reviews.reviewer: Alex, Geddy, Neil, Jerry, Bobby, Phil, Brent, Mickey, Billy

reviews.reviewbody: Yea I really like the Grateful 80's.I think the 80s were some of there best years.Yea ther were some bad shows and bad Recording's but with the soundboards out know there are so many great shows to here.There were some really good shows in the 90's but but they were rare,When they were on they were really on in the 90's and then there were good shows in the 70's the only thing is some of there best songs were not out yet,But the ones that were out are some of the deads finest and the root of them and.They still were a great band back then.!The other thing is I did not like donna and I thought she just killed some of the best shows in the 70's.But I think Brent was the best Keyboardist they had,he was great so I have to say the 80's were the best and 89 was there best yearI think.This show does not do the band good bad recording kinda and they were a little off.I have to give it a 2.The night before was a good show I thought.

This is a very short, unenthusiastic show with very few highlights.  The show starts off nicely with a decent Jack Straw that has good energy with some vocal flubs.  Dupree's follows and while always a nice surprise, Jerry's voice is croaking and cracking all over the place.  He kind of sounds like he's dying.  Musically well performed however.  Minglewood is a disaster with lots of mistakes and uninspired playing.  Jerry's vocals improve a bit for Brown Eyed Women but he makes lots of lyric flubs.  Esau is one of the highlights of the set with strong vocals and instrumentation.  Bird Song has some troubles in the beginning, especially craggy vocals and lyric flubs.  The jam however takes off nicely and turns this into a serviceable rendition.  The Bucket>Might As Well set-ender is very sloppy and lacks energy.

The second set is a bit of an improvement but it is terribly short with very little jamming.  Truckin' is strong but the post vocal jam is cu short, segueing into a decent Terrapin.  Jerry's vocals are a bit rough but it's a pretty good rendition.  Woman Smarter is the highlight of the set.  It is long and Bobby sings a bit of Iko in the middle.  The post Space jam consists of only two songs, a subpar Throwing Stones and a godawful Touch with brutal vocals and lyric flubs aplenty.  This show is a huge let down.

I sadly remember this show all too well.  While it's not in Boreal territory, it's mighty close.  Even with a very cool Bird Song > Bucket > Might As Well closer for the first set, it's still meh.  I was ready to write the band off after this night.  Fortunately the Greek shows in June turned me around.

They have a snap to their sound in 1985- kinda like STATIC ELECTRICITY. ---Not sure when it was but when the band purchased those huge glass round clear electric charged globes that they had up on stage--- I thought man that perfectly captures what the Dead are all about. The electric current would change colors and patterns based on what the band was playing and by the music's intensity. 
We actually found those orbs downtown in N.Y.C at an art gallery and we put our hands up to them and the electricity would follow our hands wherever they went.
Anyway,I digress-- let's get on with the show, let's go!
Solid Jack Straw-  they throw in a ONE MORE TIME during the lyrics. Me thinks that is a slight nod to the 20th anniversary. But I don't remember that added lyric anywhere else in 85. (I will have to keep listening)
Anyway, Dupree's is hot, they seemed to play it pretty regularly in 85.
Minglewood-So hot live and the ladies dug it as well.
Listen to Garcia getting going for B.E. Women.
 I never  could hear this live without crying tears of joy. Such a sweet tune. Garcia could struggle with this one at times lyrically but when he put the metal to the pedal it was pure bliss.
"Lilah Jones went to meet her God..."
----Hey Bobby how bout a rock and roll song?
ESAU- one of the treats of 1985.
Great story song with plenty of twists and turns. 
All kinds of discussions about the lyrics on this tune.
Altamont, Vietnam, Old Testament, The Apocalypse
 I just dig the way this tune has its own distinct sound. 
"I dreamed one night, we were holding hands,,
Shadowboxing the Apocalypse and wandering/watering
the land"
Bird Song-  this tune kept getting more jammy as the years went on. Now nothing is ever going to top the early years where Bird Song is so psychedelic it literally is a mini TRIP. but they jammed heavy on this tune in the 80s and 90s! No exception here as they start exploring the cosmos..
Brent-is bopping along.
Bucket-This song was good before it got the MTV treatment. After MTV if cell phones had been around people would have been taking selfies of "Me at a Dead show as the Grateful Dead play that HELL IN A BUCKET song from MTV"
Anyway, can't blame the song. It has a good riff, fun to dance and as my buddy gave me this warning, "it is about vengeance, man" Anyway if you have heard any of Joan Baez folky tunes this song should make you at least chuckle. And besides this is the video gave the AFLAC duck his start.
"Hey Sally, Ride, Ride, Ride"
Mighty Swell--Might as Well--You weren't dancing for this, you were already passed out.
Some Laryngitis for the JER man- went with the territory in 1985. He just sings right thru it.
Set 2
Truckin' -Always like this tune opening a set. Some Chula Vista cruiser during the opening lyrics. This is Not an oversized version but they tear it up. "Ain't it a shame"
Dig Brent singing "Sometimes the lights all shining on me"
Important thing is they jam out of 'truckin' not just shut it down. And really a nice segue into TERRAPIN. Whatever Garcia is lacking on his vocals he is more than sharp on the guitar.
Inspiration, due me rightly?
Not a huge fan of Women are Smarter. i think it has more to do with the placement of the tune. Plus Aiko is always much preferred in my book but since they are interwoven in that New Orleans sound the basic dance beat is the same. Hey we get some AIKO thrown in with a CHINESE NEW YEAR --Gung Hey Fat Chow! Pretty short pre-drums and not much going on after drums with Space>Throwing>Touch E) Johnny B 
HMMN-Solid 4 for set one
Not quite a 4 for set two (is that diplomatic enough)
Maybe they had plans for after the gig?
A reluctant 3
I was there. I thought maybe we'd seen the on-stage break-up of the Grateful Dead. But yeah then there were many good years to come. It really was that bad tho...

Heating up for sure, wanted more from Jack Straw.  Mingelwood with a good Brent portion of the jam. My brother Esau almost never worked. Bird Song and we are back!  Great version.  And I love the 80s style of birdsong.  Very short second set, excellent terrapin jam where they explored a bit, do we need Iko Iko and woman smarter back to back nights? even did a verse of Iko. Super week after space, throwing stones touch and grey and straight to the Johnny be Goode encore.   Second set was a lets get this over with setlist.  Seemed to be trying to refine some of the In the Dark live material, not to great affect. 

Show had glimpses of the band cohesion coming around but a lot of shaky playing and missed signals.

reviews.reviewtitle: the collection just keeps getting bigger

reviews.reviewbody:
Just streamed this, and then downloaded it. What great sound and quality. Quite a show for the collection. I think it is well worth the listen and definetly worth adding in the collection.

As stated above, much thanks to Etree for posting these shows.

~Dan
Sloppy & uninspired playing, dreadful vocals. I'm heading back to the 70's, thanx.

I have to agree with the first reviewer.  The vocals aren't that great on this.  Jerry sounds "drugged" up and strains quite a bit.  Mayabe it was just not a good night for him.  The recording sounds fine but Jerry sounds not all that great.   Just my opinion.  He did much better perfomrances.  But still kudos for posting this..  The Dead are soo cool.  I'll take them  "warts and all".

In listening to this awesome sbd I note that it is really Bobby that is having vocal issues. Sounds to me as if he has a cold or something to that affect. The sound quality otherwise is top notch and is a welcome addition to my shn archive. I do remember this was the year Jerry's voice started failing a bit but remember it being in the summer tour. But I could be wrong.
reviews.reviewtitle: Jerrynot at his best??? Isnt it really Bobby you mean????

reviews.reviewbody:
These shows were the first after Jerry's bust in GG park. The second set here is phenomenal. 
The SBD quality just makes this show hum along. The scarlet intro is one of the hottest of this year. Great Fire, too. A nice night and a typical hot set list for the tour. 

I am close to giving this 5 stars, which I could do for sound quality but the show just does not make it to that status level. That being said it is a great download and I have listened to every note thus far. Check out the 9.5 minute West LA and day Tripper, nto to mention the cold rain...I cranked this on the way to work today.  You will too once you hear it. 

bravo boys bravo!!!
Well balanced mix, excellent sound overall, pretty good show, not great, some might argue going through the motions somewhat, but basically a winner.

Not only are Jerry's vocals of the "drugged-up" type (I think we all know what that sounds like), but take a listen to Weir's voice.  EVEN WORSE!  Ouch, that along with the 80's sluggish drumming, I'll pass on the d/l.

You all made me tap deep in my vault for this one...Having been at this show, this show was a Grateful Dead show - say no more.  The vocals of Bobby and Jerry were fine.  However, was energy level down for the boys, yes, but then again we just called it layed back "west coast style" of which Dead had a tendacy to do till the end.

I dont get the gripe.  This is smooth and deep, a work of art.  Very laidback but purposeful.  Everyone is exploring the music.  The second set is full of beautiful explorations.  Meticulous and balanced.  This is 4.5 star art.

If you can sit through this show you are too stoned to move to click it off. Day Tripper is a Train Wreck. West LA - wake me when it's over... oh it is? Someone woke the band... it's mama tried. It was a good try boys. Big river keeps moving - not bad I guess. T.Jed - goes no where. I'm not going to go through the rest but move on to some shows from 78 or 87-88-89

Yeah, the vocals on Day Tripper were painful, but so were most of the infrequent covers Ive heard them do here and there (Satisfaction and Baba ORiley come to mind). In spite of Bobbys voice being shot, great mix and sound quality  very crisp. First set is mellow. Second set definitely makes up for deficiencies in the first. This is one of those shows that takes you back...Thanks.
Brutal vocals.  Ouch!

Jerry's voice may be a little ragged but it's nothing compared to Bobby's rusty frog gargle. I guess the show must go on eh? But they should have taken this night off if they were that sick. The playing isn't terrible but nothing too inspired happens. It's obvious they weren't feeling well and weren't focused. Jerry has some nice runs in Playing and Scarlett but the drummers bring most of the procedings way down to planet Boring with their indifferent thud/wack pokey playing. They take it up a notch for the encore, but it's too little too late. There's no magic and no reason to listen to this show.

This is vocally, one of the worst performances I've heard from the Dead.  We all know about Jerry's voice/health problems at this stage, but on this night Bobby's voice is even worse.  He obviously is sick and probably shouldn't be singing.  

Cold Rain and Snow stars the show off with good energy but one of the worst performances in the history of the band follows.  During Day Tripper Bobby's voice is absolutely atrocious and is cracking and croaking the entire song.  Musically this performance is awful and vocally it is even worse.  It is very difficult to even get through.  Absolutely horrid!  Fortunately, a mellow West L.A. Fadeaway improves things.  This version is very laid back but I love it.  Bob's voice is slightly improved for the cowboy duo of Mama Tried>Big River but not by much.  The jam in Big River is at least energetic and enthusiastic.  The rest of the set is lackluster and pretty boring.

The second set is a vast improvement ans starts off with a very nice, long and jammed out Scarlet>Fire.  This is the highlight of the evening.  Some vocals flubs but the playing is intense with fiery leads by Garcia and interesting group improvisation.  The Playin' that comes next is interesting because the lyric section is mercifully but short and quickly dissolves into a long spacey jam.  Decent but it doesn't really go anywhere too interesting.  Post Space is a bit anticlimactic with a standard version of the Wheel followed by a long Black Peter.  For some unknown reason, with all of Bob's vocal troubles, they decide to end the show with an eleven minute Lovelight including a lengthy rap.  The playing is passionate but Bob sounds like death. They should have gone with something else or closed it out with a Jerry tune.  This avoids one star because of the Scarlet>Fire.

There are some dropped lyrics and both Garcia and Weir have rough voices (that at moments seem to pop right back into great form), but the playing is fiery and the show is full of wonderful moments.

This show is NOT lifeless. Scrappy, but definitely has some great playing.

I think it's pretty interesting how they try on a song like Day Tripper, play it a handful of times and then decide that it does nothing for them. In this particular instance there really isn't much room to grow beyond the basic theme, so why bother?

By far the best of the run.  However, I will say I have never heard Bobby's voice like this. He must be legit sick, not party sick.

1st set was mediocre overall, but West La and mama>big river were nice versions.

Scarlet>Fire is the best music they conjured up this 3 night run and it was a meaty version. Playing also then explored some territory. post space was again kinda weak continuing the trend of the year so far. 

This 3 night run was marred by shaky voices, forgotten lyrics and some missed links musically. But one can tell they are trying to put their foot back into that comfortable shoe and shake off some bad vibes and personal lows that the boys endured since new years '84.  The inklings of a different sound is in there and you can see it germinating.  Just need to tightening it up.  Rhythm section were finding the pocket way more on night 3 then 1, that is a good sing.  Lots more to come from this year.

The sound is not quite as warm as my analog copy, but it sounds good nonetheless. Begin your 85 collection here if you have not already-4 stars on recording, 5 on performance

Here's some cover-art for this show: 
http://www.toddalbert.com/music/cover_art/

I am glad I made the trip out to see this show.  It was a bit out of the way for us NC folk, especially after seeing the previous shows in MD, PA, and NY.  The city was better than I expected.  I thought it would be a rust bucket, but it was nice almost like Gotham City.  The people in the area were also very friendly.  The show was great.  I saw the comment about sounds in the mix but I do remember quite a few technical errors during the show.  I thought the Dead were playing strong.  The sound quality of this recording is pretty good.  I really enjoyed the Wharf Rat and The brokedown brokedown was a riot. A real high point of the tour with all the red gel in the air.

This show is damn good but the sound quality is a little suspect. There is some crackling throughout and the mix is not quite right. I need more Phil! It sounds a bit airy. That seems to be a prob in a lot of 80's SBD's. Any way don't let my review discourage you. This is a very good show and worth a DL.

I laughed and laughed when Jerry seemed like he was already singing Brokedown before he really started singing it.  The "Hello.  Sounded good didn't it?" had me on the ground rolling.  Fun show!  Definitely worth the listen..

One pane of glass in the window...
pretty good show but i believe that when screwing up brokedown which i think if memory serves me right happened again at the rocks this year he starts in the wrong key then aborts

Went to the Merriweather shows and this one, very different, inside for first time on tour? Merriweather rocked both nights, this one was ethereal and spacey with Phils base lines bouncing around the dome. The crackling in the recording was the soundboard, which had a bunch of water dumped on it in Hershey when the canopy failed during a deluge. Only time I really liked MBTR. Wharf rat was also really good, there unfortunately aren't any recordings which capture the sound the way I remember it but it is worth a listen for the unique mood.

Carwing wrote a perfect review of this show.  I saw that whole tour, and Ventura. Missed the Greeks, went in '86.  This was a very solid well-executed show after the merriweather 7.1 blow-out.  I agree with the wharf rat, nice crazy fingers too.  '85 was great, I know too many heads plder than me that agree to give any of these non-'85 people any credibility.  Most of them were probably not at the shows and go only by the recordings.  Thats what you do for The Cure, not the Grateful Dead.

Funny how long ago , the strange trip -good sound good night. They stopped doing the Lost Sailor •Saint of Circumstance combo soon after. Bob in a pink Alligator T-Shirt ( classic) . The encore - Jerry Garcia " Hello - sounded good didn't it . We all started playin .... Blah blah blah . "The Throwin Stones • Turn on Your Lovelight is great. The Terrapin Station is fabulous as is the whole first set. Woman are Smarter ( ManSmart Woman are Smarter)  second set opener is a treat.Crazy Fingers!!!!!          Set 1

reviews.reviewtitle: Great  show this was my first.

reviews.reviewbody:
If you like shows from 1985, then you will like this show.  If you don't like shows from 1985, then you won't like this show.  Why?  Because this show typifies 1985 - a lot of straightforward, hard-rockin' (for the Dead) songs, but nothing that really gets totally, jazzily out there.

I enjoyed the tail end of Jack Straw where the entire band stops playing and Jerry plays the intro into It Must Have Been the Roses - it was just a brief little moment of crisp, clear calm playing and then the band picks up the new tune.  Very well done.  It Must Have Been the Roses in general is a first set highlight, and Cassidy ends with the typical 1980's pizazz.  

In the second set, the jam at the end of Terrapin, Drums, and then a smoking Wharf Rat were the highlights for me - the Wharf Rat is  especially good. 

One big complaint about this particular transfer is that Revolution and Brokedown Palace are tracked in the middle of the show, when they belong at the end.  The show gets three stars for the playing, but the incorrect order is really annoying.  And for you audiophiles out there, this recording has a lot of noise - not enough to bother me, but I can see where it would distract some listeners.

i loved this show but being a hometown show and not visiting the parents i mgotta lot of crap i loved this whole year yeah sure Jer's voice got to be a bit harsh but he still had the guitar which he played very tight i loved this Jack Straw  and the Wharf Rat was killer i just loved everything about 85 prolly cuz it was first year of touring but still u could buy like season tickets to a tour or run or whatever even walk up to the box office like in the fall at Hollywood great times i am so so glad i got to experience the total package  great music great people and even greater scene

Sound is good but some crackling here and there..This reminds me of the summer of 87 when they played indoors at Roanoke..it kind of throws you for a loop when you want to be outdoors..but what da hey!! still a good show and worth a listen..I want to give it a 3.5, but since I can't I'll go up to a 4 star..so please..GIVE IT A WHIRL>Forever Grateful>Forever DEAD!!!!
Wharf Rat

I was at this show, and ...
reviews.reviewbody:
enjoyed it thoroughly, but it's pretty blase compared to some other shows played that tour (Blossom, SPAC, Hershey, Merriweather 1).  Still, every song is very well played, even if there isn't any real jamming to speak of.  Particularly strong are Cassidy (though short), Saint, Terrapin, and Wharf Rat.

Just want to add:  It was such a relief and a joy to hear Jerry sounding SO MUCH BETTER on vocals than when I heard him at the Spectrum that spring.

Good show.

reviews.reviewbody: I could swear that the dates are mixed up for '85 Red Rocks. I remember this show as AFTER the night they played 'Hey Jude' and 'Dear Mr. Fantasy', but there are several copies of 9/7/85 with that show's setlist. Anyone else there who could corroborate?
Definately the 2nd night of 3

Someone actually thought this was the last night.  Unbelieveable.  9.7 was one of the big nights of '85, after Phil singing on Tom Thumb's, the whole Day Tripper thing and of course the unbelieveable Greek shows.  And every night of the summer tour after the Greek.  (Those were some of the hottest of my 230-plus shows, especially Cinci 6.24).  I mean come on man, everybody remembers them breaking out the Hey Jude coda at the last night at the Rocks.  Unfortunately they kept doing it in the late '80's, to me it was very lame without the sponataneity of the debut.  Just like Do it in the Road at Merriweather '84, should have left it at that.  It seems like the more reviews I read, the more I feel like an old time Head, and my first show was not until '79!  Did anyone who accesses this site actually see the Dead before the whole Touch of Gray / In the Dark era ruined everything?!?!  If so I would love to hear from you!!

While these shows are certainly very good for the time, I have to agree with Lesh69. There is a lot of love for post '85, more than the period merits. I find the rating system for this era to be out of whack, I hove found very few 5 star shows after 1985.The last 10 years, for me were dissapointing, and it was obvious that Jerry was declining and it was hard and sad to watch him deteriorate before our eyes. It does seem that most of the folks here are younger heads who love late Dead and appreciate the classics as well. While I certainly understand the propensity to prefer the shows you were at, I think there is far too much love for later shows here, compared to what IMHO is one of the best periods, Fall 1979-Fall 1982. .

If it weren't for the next days awsome show I 'm not sure I would have ever forgiven the horrible performance this day!

Jerry left the stage to go do a "spoonful" and I will never forget turning my back on him because he was such a mess as was most of the music.
reviews.reviewtitle: one of the most disappointing shows of all time

reviews.reviewbody: One of the most disappointing shows of all time? I'm listening now. Great energy, Brent is smokin', tight!Most Disappointing would be the '95 run. Sure beats Vince fartin' all over the place. 4 stars, just to spite the poster below me.

This was one of those absolute perfect shows in person: the crowd, the weather - and one that sounded different a few months later on tape, as usual. It was also the shortest 1st set I ever saw; but the brevity didn't keep it from being one of my most played 1st sets of '85-'89. I wore that freaking tape out. I think it was because I liked the center section, because it was one of the lowest gens I had (I had lucked into the sacks_28164 source close to the master), and because I wasn't the collector I became down the road. But by today's standards, the show hasn't really been done justice by sources. A matrix is needed and a Miller would be nice (nudge). These were 2pm shows, changed after locals in a nearby village had a council meeting trying to end the 4-day circus of the previous 3 years, conceding to an earlier showtime (tie-dyed nappers in yards, some sort of bizarre picketing for "miracles". Not in my backyard!). A skeleton crew readied the Boulder Events Center in case of rainout. What other touring band did this? Few-to-none that I've heard tell. First Set. Helena warms up and gets better. Jer's funny, warning "Okay Bobby, not too fast now! Be very careful - watch out Bobby!" Bobby liked to punch his song and so did Billy - not so much Phil & Jer. Paybacks the next show. FWIW, this is a personal fave version of Sugaree, and the start of a great middle set sequence (my wife at the time named our puppy after this Sugaree). I love Bobby and Jer's choices here (a matrix would be nice - Bobby is more audible on the AUDs). Bobby's Slide Practice™ aside, it's a great version of It's All Over Now and a nicet Bird Song. Not true for the rough El Paso and average Dough Knees. Second Set. The entire set is uptempo (if yr source is accurate). It was probably Healy that burped at the start of Iko, because it went over the PA. The set gets going in the last minute of Looks Like Rain and into a good He's Gone. The drummers are anxious and Jer leaves as Phil and Bobby go into Spoonful. It's the 6th of 8 in '85 but they're in and out pretty quick. Drums>Space were showpieces during the last few Red Rocks runs, with Mickey bringing and setting up many of his toys. This Wheel stuck out in person but on tape there are better '85s. Black Peter is the opposite. Gold. Stones>NFA is above average but there's some drummer soup. US Blues is one of the best '85s. 1st Set:  B- 2nd Set: B Overall = 3½ stars Highlights: Sugaree - it's a grower Black Peter - Jer was looking forward to this; drummers comply U.S. Blues - uptempo rave up SOURCES: There's only one SBD source (weiner_12181), and it has slow wow and pitch errors and needs EQ. Correct these and yr fine. The first set has a very slow wobble and needs -1% speed correction for All Over Now, Bird Song & El Paso. Conversely, the entire second set plays slow and needs +1%. The sacks_28164 is a great AUD. The mccue-ford AUD runs too slow.

I don't think I've heard this since I was at the show.  The recording's quite clean, and it sounds like they were having fun, even though both sets were short. I like El Paso's circus intro and the great Phil run after the guitar lead. The extra drums in Spoonful after Jerry left the stage were interesting, too. Does anyone out there know whose belch that was at the start of Iko-Iko?
http://estimatedprofits.blogspot.com/2009/10/1985-09-06-red-rocks-amphitheatre.html

Yes, the stars aligned the next night on 9/7 
and 21 years later it is still that 3rd night
 that gets all the traffic and press
 but this show is not slack.
I'll go with 'Mind Wonderin' and his review.
 I was at these shows!!!
Although truthfully all I can remember is the 3rd night, but that does not mean
 there was not good music the first two shows.
Remember the expression ' if you can remember the sixties you weren't really there'. 
Well the Dead carried the 60's with them on tour wherever they went.
As a head and addressing another review from 2007-the whole Jerry going down hill story line is old and tired and truthfully extremely disrespectful to his memory.
Should Jerry have taken better care of himself?
Should i? Should you? should everyone?
Should musicians not do and get hooked on smack?
Ever get high?
Should Jerry have
taken better care with the 
type 2 adult onset Diabetes?
Hope you never have to find out.
Anyway, off the soap box and back to the show.
USED TO LOVE HER a great tune for the boys,
They played it somewhat regularly 
during this time period.
I am wondering what I was doing during this show.
 I vaguely remember a mosh pit
 but no clue if that was an actual experience or not.
The Bird Song is really the cosmic departure point
 for this first set.
 You know listening to this and thinking about the beauty of Red Rocks. It is kinda overwhelming.
 I was so young and headstrong and full of reckless abandon.I wanted to just tour full time, but i had school and a night job. I just got in shows wherever i could , whenever I could. Mostly East Coast but occasionally furthur...
I know folks were down on the TOUCH heads but aside from the frat boy scene , many of those college girls kept the tour rolling--- pouring in all kinds of disposable income for everything from hippie jewelry to stir fry, grill cheese,,, 
Only thing i held against anyone is if they tried to talk over the music. Other than that- (well gate crashing, that sucked as well.)
"All i know , she sang a little while and then flew off"
Tight El Paso- Garcia throwing all kinds of lightning bolts. If you have ever been on the hills overlooking El Paso you know that like Red Rocks there is an amazing vibe to both places.
Don't Ease-Great for dancing, sometimes a bit of shock if you were thinking there might be a few more tunes coming. Oh, well say the old folks, it goes to show ,you never can tell...solution--Dance Harder!!!

Aiko- I have been listening to some of those Aiko's from late 70's with Donna and just loving them post drums. this is bee-bopping along , Jerry a little off on his lyrics, but guys jump in to keep it going.
My theory on this run is the weekend was so great as has been mentioned by many reviewers that by the time you get to Sunday there is such an air of expectation. If the Dark Star had been in rotation or the St. Stephen we would have gotten it that day.
Anyway, Looks Like Rain, pretty ironic because the sunshine was on everyone's mind. My thoughts on this tune were strictly 1st set. Perhaps Weir ought to play this in the closer ballad spot-- might go over?
The board messes with Weir's vocal levels on LLR. 
"Sometimes the sky is blue, you never think , no rain could f@ck with you"
In the later years I couldn't hear He's Gone without thinking about loved ones lost. Be it family, friends and of course in the GD universe.
Here my only connection was to great version in my tape collection. I have actually gotten much more upbeat about this song over the years. They tended to jam in and out of it. The harmonies were great especially when phil was in the mix. plus I now focus on the NOTHING LEFT TO DO BUT SMILE SMILE SMILE...
Remember the time they opened the Second Set in RFK with He's Gone!
rather than the Good friends , we had, good friends we lost...Nothings gonna bring em back...
Spoonful sometimes after He's Gone and other times after Truckin' It seemed to me to be not very regularly played (ie-not in rotation) but did show up all the way into the 90's post Brent.
Drums>Space>Wheel--(heavy drums, light wheel)
Black Peter-kinda surprised this is right after the Wheel. Not a super dramatic version but good.
Stones>N.F.A- this got somewhat played. It was pretty right on for the time period. T Stones-- is now somewhat dated ,It worked live back then-- kinda like some of Brent's tunes now don't seem as weighty.
The N.F.A gets a pretty good treatment here.
Those Not Fade chants as a crowd were pretty special.
U.S. Blues-good tune for Red Rocks which makes all those symbols, rules and regulations seem rather useless.

This recording of a lovely show isn't something that the seasoned, jaded critic is going to jump off the second level of the Coliseum for to grab a copy of. Nevertheless, I think it has a cool drippy, dropply sound that is quite entertaining and reminiscent of the way some of our ears caught the music as we spun in the halls. Perfection is relative, tastes vary, but I would be ever so weary of the words"never should be circulated." I let it circulate in my cells and they quite enjoyed it. (Matthew 7:1)

I usually say "anything is better than nothing" as far as having an available soundboard bootleg of a show but, I agree with mom.  This has to be one of the worst uses of noise reduction I have ever heard. Making it NOT crispy.  The first and second sets are out of tune with each other as well.  A common problem with cassette gens.  I appreciate some of the things people do to try to make listening more enjoyable.  I think after all these years though, we all have our own equipment to make things better to suit our own taste.  This might have been a three or four star recording originally, first generation.  Maybe some day someone will post a better board with a better lineage.

That being said, this is a sub par performace for the boys in 1985.  It has it's moments but, bad song transitions. A lot of them.

Two stars because it used to be a soundboard, could have been four!
I think it sounds pretty cool...

Way over shadowed by the previous night but very worth the time and effort.  Well played and well mixed by Healy.  I like Jerry's sound and his picking is sharp, especially the 2nd solo during UJB.  Bob does break out the slide a little too much but it's not out of tune.  Also not listed is a little Playin Jam out of China Doll into the drums.

Morning Dew lovers need this show.  I have always liked the way they spaced into this Dew and Phil has a couple blowouts during the middle jam that must have driven Healy nuts.  Great dynamics and while the end is not as long as Barton Hall it is very moving.  "Guess it doesn't matter, anyway!"

It's a shame that the good folks at Grateful Dead Productions didn't have the foresight to release this show as a companion to DP21 as they did with the May '77 releases that made up DP29 because this is one great show.  

As noted in the liner notes to DP21, there was some overall weirdness that started at the Halloween show in South Carolina that carried over and northward to Richmond for the two night run there.  This review is limited to my opinions and impressions of the 2d set.

Iko starts off on a very jangly vibe, real loose and bumpy, with some solid Garcia vocals and Mydland shadings.  Weir shifts gears quickly and affirmatively with a well-delivered Estimated Prophet that melts into an outro jam for several minutes before landing at Uncle John's doorstep.  To me, Garcia was a double threat.  Emotionally, his voice leant poignancy, vibrancy, creativity, and many other adjectives to the proceedings, and naturally, the notes he pulled from Wolf, Tiger, and his other axes speak for themself.  Here its the vocal lead that really gets me going, and this is particularly so during a great China Doll that Garcia lends a real contemplative perspective to, hitting the words hard, really letting them sink in, and then flavoring his vocal stew with the memorable leads we all know and love.

Drums>Space continues the rub of buzzing, clicking, and other unusual sounds that is the signature sound of this segment from '85.  Space melts into a very strong Morning Dew that again, Jerry just imbues with a force, power and energy that only he could provide.  As might be expected, the Stones>Lovelight seems a wee bit anti-climactic, but are both solid.  Baby Blue is a great encore, and were it not for the prior night, I think this show would get far greater attention.  

One note on your various downloading choices.  This is a crystal clear SBD, with an outstanding mix.  I had an AUD version for many years that sounded like the boys were in a canyon, so for those that like that audience mix, give in and grab a top notch SBD.  

I'd give it 4.5 if it were an option, but since it's not, I'm going 4 stars, and a high recommendation.

ENJOY

PS .. It goes without saying that the people at the Archive have literally fulfilled the dreams of many DeadHeads by giving us what is essentially the "skeleton key" into the Vault.  I cannot thank you all enough for putting all of this wonderful music up on the Internet and making it available to the masses.

This was also my first show and I went with no clue what the Dead were or what type of music they played. I walked around and checked people out for most of the first set but by the time the second set started I was glued to the stage. At the time I was into 80's punk music and reggae (went to a lot of Bad Brains shows growing up) and I didn't even know a live band could sound like that. By the time Bobby ripped into Estimated I had found my new idol. I was hooked. The Dew out of Space is the highlight in my opinion. This was a perfect spot for the song and it always added an extra touch to an already dramatic song. The second set of this show is a great example of solid Dead. They have gone at it with a lot more ferocity at other times but this second set is clean and prime like a studio release. Good SB should be easy to find of this night. The previous night is available on Dick's Picks, which brings up my only bone to pick with this show. Being that this was my first show and had the choice of going to Fri or Sat night I picked Sat. How could I have known that my first show could have been the all time schorcher that is 11/1/85. If you've never heard it, get it. The Band goes off and pulls out one of the craziest second sets they ever played.

First tape I ever had (~86).  It was crusty, hissy, and choppy, but never failed to please.  Hearing the Space into Dew is what I consider quintessential, natural Dead.  IMHO, it was never about THE SHOW, it was about what makes you keep coming back for more;  that instance when the boys brought it all together when the game plan busted and their natural ability to create art would take over.  And for me, it is the transition into Dew here.  Nice to hear a clean SBD version.  However, the audience hissy'ness is still preferable.  I guess it is nostalgic for me.

You know this is the beauty of this site.  you can go to a show that has been downloaded 50,000 times then go to the show before or after, and it be just as good if not better. I LOVE THIS SITE! Any way this first set is grate. I would have like to have seen an "all over now" in place of "CC rider". but that is just an opinion.
  The secon set was amazing as well.  very nice song selection here. Like the "Aiko",Estimated,U.J.B.,China doll! Magnificent.  then you have the DEW out of drums.  and the placement of morning dew says to me that it was all emotion and feeling right then.  Jerry wanted to play it right then! I love it!  a great addition to your 85' collection for sure.           

                  peace.

Sidebar @ Sedula, Like these reviews everyone has their own opinion, but the reviews and ratings are about the show. Casting a 'rating' based on someone else personal opinion is a great disservice to all of us. Like him or not Bobby was a founding member and HUGE contributor to the over all success and longevity of the GD. Fortunately in this case my review of you as a class A loser is consistent with the review of the great show. Five Stars!!!

First off-- this is a great show, so don't take the criticism too seriously. 

Highlights-- Dupree's and China Doll

Bertha is a great start to a great show. Good rendition. Greatest Story, though it ain't one of my favorite songs, is excellent. Dupree's is inexplicably great. CC Rider is really good and would be better if Bob's slide solo were louder. I think it's Weir. It is great slide playing. Speaking of the sound, other than what I just mentioned, the sound on this show is outstanding: 5 stars. Althea is great musically, but what's a Dead show w/o Jerry forgetting a few lyrics? Esau-- another one that's not a fav-- is well played. Candy Man is excellent. Let it Grow is good. Iko is fun as usual. Estimated is particularly tight! Uncle-- don't mind more forgotten lyrics-- this Uncle John's Band flows like a winding stream, beautifully!!! China Doll is gorgeous, even better than usual methinks. Oh, it includes a brief Playin' tease. Dew? Well, it's Morning Dew-- what more do you want? Throwing Stones w/ a brief NFA tease and Love Light are just fine. The Baby Blue encore is a nice way to end this one.

As much as I appreciate Bobby, I am hearing Sedula. It can go both ways. Abrupt entries into rockers when the Dew ends is in bad taste. The Dew should simply end unless they are going back into UJB>Playing of course. Rochester 1980 is a classic case in point. With Sugar Magnolia starting up the lone Iko>Dew could not be properly acknowledged. Lovelight should have been played when Garcia was good. Estimated solos should never be interrupted to wrap up your song etc...

reviews.reviewbody: There were hundreds of people outside with tickets trying to get in as show started and these administrative morons had no idea what the hell they were doing. Standing outside with a ticket hearing Bertha and you couldn't get in the door. People chanting the Who...The Who......that rececenly had a show where a number of people had been trampled to death. Very ugly scene outside that night. The show was good...organization was not. They were banned from Richmond after that by the powers that be which is damn shame cause it wasn't the the fans that caused the problem. JGB did play there in 93...didn't see it but heard it was the best show of the tour. Again...shame cause they were going to play at the racetrack in summer of 87 but they were banned. They played Roanoke Virginia instead. Both good shows.

I'm always kind of amused by the comments regarding the sound quality of the board recording.  This night for example has a review that says Healy was on his game.  The straight from the board tape is a reflection of the building, not Healy's game.  None of the sports arenas were designed for music and their acoustics were mostly both awful and unique.  Tuning the PA to overcome the building's shortcomings was the magic and that's why some board tapes sound so weird.

Show was amazing in the sweet spot in FOB. 
My tape is uncut. Not gonna check to see what happened here, but few tapes were uncut this night. Richmond rocked. Gotta love old brick buildings.

I'd love to find a recording of the tuning for 2nd set from the moment they went on stage. I used to have Bob Messina's audience recording which captures a beautiful keyboard flourish. It really sets the tone. One thing that the board recording does not capture is the way Phil shredded the PA during the Dew. Later, I heard that he'd discovered how to crack the stack during summer tour and they were going to replace the whole PA after Worcester so he just went at it with no mercy.

reviews.reviewbody: First of all, it was nice to have the Dead play so close to home for me.  This show smoked from the beginning to end.  The Bucket, Sugaree, El Paso & Dupree's were all peak performances.  The second set had two surprise openers of a hot Tennesee Jed followed by a rocking Cumberland.  Miracle was hot too and Crazy Fingers was sweet.  Comes a Time was also a highlight and the energy just exploded with Gimmee Some Lovin'.  Phil and Brent had a nice vocal rap in the end that went into a short jam that Jerry cut off to do Truckin'.  Peter was good and Good Loving was hot  One thing that this recording doesn't have is Bobby taking the microphone off the mike stand during Good Loving and walking around during his rap.  Day Job was played well too though most of us were so sick of that song by that time.
So... Did anyone else go see Peter Popov heal people the next day at the civic center next door?

i tripped (on acid, first time) at this show with philrmonic below.  man, open the 2nd set w/ Tennessee Jed? of course, i thought it was because i was tripping that they did that...my buddy Al lost his glasses during cumberland. and i saw hopi sand paintings on the inside of my eyelids...and yes faith healer peter popov was saving souls next door to the arena all afternoon the next day...being the curious folks we were, we watched pete save every sucker who went up there...every so often there'd be a deadhead getting saved...too weird, or not weird enough...see "hopi sandpainting" reference above
this sounds really good.  i wasn't as taken by the performance as the rest of the reviewers.

I know that it is not always the quantity of the show that matters, but this is one of the shortest shows I have come across. DNA but would have been bummed that they did not close out with Tennessee Jed and Cumberland in the first set instead of opening with it for set 2. 
I guess it was a novelty?
Pre drums is 27 minutes.

Kaiser 2/20 was shorter overall (only 8 songs in the first set and LL Rain barely over 10 min). But in this show, Bucket was roughly as long as nearly every second set song. (Crazy Fingers aside).

I think the show is average for 1985. Probably had some hot moments but not in league with Philly, Springfield, 'Toga, Richmond, etc... .

It's true that the show's a bit short, and they didn't really pull anything out special, but what they played, they played well! The recording is of mixed quality, changing throughout from warm to bright, but never bad.

I did not miss many shows in '85, 4 total...these shows sucked...the worst of the year after Boreal and Philly 4.6 (4.7 and 8 were very hot)..band was tired from the killer East Coast Fall Tour...the next week at the Kaiser was scorching hot, some of my favorite ever.

These shows still beat anything after '86.

reviews.reviewbody:
Though this show didn't top yesterday, the first set was extremely rocking and there were no low points in the first set.

He's Gone was cool but Jerry's guitar was halfway off when Bobby started Spoonful, Jerry hung in there and faced his amp for the whole song and played little.  He left for drums just as the song ended but Brent hung around to give us another tune before drums.  Not too much happend afer drums
First set was rock solid. 2nd saw a bit of an energy dip. BUT, Never Trust/Good Times is the best I have ever heard. And frankly, so is the Throwing Stones/NFA combo!

well, everybody has a first show, and this was mine (#1 of 99).  shrooms, alcohol, bud, etc and I didn't know any dead tunes. "it's all over now" and "NFA" were the only songs i heard before.

first set was clean, crisp and lively...

china rider>samson>hes gone>spoonful>good times was awesome before drums. was ready to rock out during the encore but jerry lullabied us with "baby blue", kept me wanting more....
98 more to be exact!
Are you kidding me? The mississippi halfstep, the minglewood, the stagger lee, the friend of devil, the big railroad, the looks like rain, this is one of the best first sets I've ever heard.

Brent sneaks another one in...there is a real preponderance in 1985 of misbegotten Brent tunes in that twilight zone between the first half of the second set and drums.  Feels like everybody's just kinda going their own way...

Spoonful>Good Times
Weir has a nice delivery on Spoonful
that and Smokestack Lightning
that is a pretty serious blues 2 shot.
All of those pre-drumz Brent tunes 
did pay dividends by 89/90 for Mydland.
Back in the day 
I was blown kinda away 
when Garcia would exit stage left
on a Brent tune pre drums
but thinking on it now
Garcia was giving Brent a chance to shine
Not sure why there is so much reverb on Brent's vocals on this tune.
